text:
▷ Government ceremony to be held on September 4 at KINTEX in Ilsan, with government awards for contributors to air quality improvement, plus side events including air environment industry exhibitions, promotions, and international symposia
▷ Minister of environment: “Through decarbonization efforts across all sectors-industry, transport, and daily life-we will improve the national average ultrafine dust concentration to below the government target of 13 ㎍/㎥ by 2029”
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Minister Cho Hyun) announced that, in celebration of the 6th International Day of Clean Air for blue skies* (Blue Sky Day, observed annually on September 7), which is both the first UN-designated international day proposed by Korea and a national commemoration day, a variety of events will be held.
* Korea first proposed the idea at the Climate Action Summit in New York (September 2019), after which the UN General Assembly at its 74th session adopted a resolution designating September 7 as the International Day of Clean Air for blue skies (December 2019). It was subsequently designated as a national commemoration day in August 2020.
The government ceremony for the 6th Blue Sky Day will be held on September 4 at 2 p.m. at KINTEX Exhibition Hall 2 in Goyang, Gyeonggi-do, and will also be broadcast online via YouTube.
The theme designated by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) for this year’s Blue Sky Day is “Racing for Air.” It connects clean air with sports, perseverance, and equity, carrying the message of shifting the focus from problems to solutions and emphasizing the need to act quickly to address the issues.
With a sense of urgency that there is no more time to delay in improving fine dust conditions and responding to climate disasters, the government has set this year’s Blue Sky Day slogan as “Racing for Air.”
Meanwhile, in commemoration of the 6th Blue Sky Day, the government will present official awards to a total of five individuals for their contributions to improving air quality.
For the Presidential Commendation, recipients include Hwang Byung-han, CEO of Kentek, the Korea Testing Certification Institute (organization), and Jeon Won-hyuk, Director of Integrated Permit System Division at the Ministry of Environment. For the Prime Minister’s Commendation, Song Sang-seok, Policy Committee Chair of Green Transportation Movement, and Lim Hyun-jung, Group Leader at Samsung Electronics, were selected as awardees.
Alongside the government ceremony, the Ministry of Environment will also hold a variety of side events, including: an international symposium on air pollutant emissions information management with participation from the public, industry, and experts; a forum on advancing air quality monitoring; a seminar on the electrification of construction and agricultural machinery; and an international workshop on the Geostationary Environment Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS).
In particular, for the first time this year, 54 exhibition booths will be operated to showcase and promote the air environment industry. These will feature a wide range of technologies and products from companies aimed at reducing emissions from transportation and industrial sites, as well as innovations in monitoring, surveillance, and policy to cut air pollutants and carbon emissions.
Ahead of the government ceremony, the Ministry of Environment carried out a variety of promotional activities to encourage public participation in Blue Sky Day and efforts to improve air quality. These included a nationwide content contest, a social media running challenge, YouTube content production, and eco-friendly engagement events in cooperation with Korea Railroad Corporation.
In addition, affiliated agencies of the Ministry of Environment and local governments will also hold various events to mark Blue Sky Day.
The Metropolitan Air Quality Management Office, together with the Seoul Metropolitan Government, will host a variety of programs on September 3 at Seoul Plaza (Lawn Plaza of the City Hall), including a Blue Sky children’s speech contest, music show, and quiz competition. The Geum River Basin Environmental Office will hold a walking challenge and conduct environmental campaigns targeting baseball stadium visitors, while local governments in Busan, Incheon, and Daejeon will organize their own commemorative ceremonies and policy forums on air quality improvement.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will also host the 5th International Forum on Transboundary Air Pollution on September 8 at the Four Seasons Hotel in Jongno-gu, Seoul, in a hybrid online-offline format to raise awareness of the need for cooperation in addressing transboundary air pollution. The event will feature in-depth discussions among domestic and international experts on topics such as the outlook for changes in East Asia’s air environment and directions for cooperation, as well as the potential for expanding joint responses to transboundary air pollution.
UN agencies also marked Blue Sky Day by promoting events and campaigns linked to sports, highlighting the severity of air pollution and the economic and social value of clean air, while encouraging global participation in efforts to improve air quality.
At the UNEP headquarters in Nairobi, Kenya, an event was held during the Nairobi Marathon to monitor air quality and provide real-time air quality information. The UN Headquarters in New York is also scheduled to host a commemorative event.
In addition, at the Asia-Pacific regional commemorative event - co-hosted by the UNEP and the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP), with support from the Embassy of Korea in Thailand - discussions will be held under the theme “Sustainable Energy for Clean Air.” The event will focus on the importance of reducing air pollution through a transition to renewable energy and achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Minister Kim Sungwhan stated, “Policies premised on fossil fuel use cannot fundamentally solve air pollution issues or address the climate disasters that could lead to the collapse of civilization.” He added, “To simultaneously resolve the climate crisis and air pollution, efforts are needed to electrify internal combustion engines and decarbonize the industrial and household sectors. Based on these efforts, we plan to improve the national average concentration of ultrafine dust (PM2.5) to below 13 ㎍/㎥ by 2029, in line with the government’s policy target.”
Minister Cho Hyun stated, “Blue Sky Day is a meaningful occasion that calls for collective human action for clean air, and our efforts toward clean air must continue.” He added, “We hope that the various events held in celebration of Blue Sky Day will provide opportunities to explore diverse avenues of international cooperation to address transboundary air pollution.”

text:
▷ Held on September 5 at Gimje Indoor Gymnasium under the theme “Plastic-Free, a promise for the earth”
▷ Listening to on-site opinions at “electric vehicle waste battery” and “solar panel waste” recycling facilities and discussing ways to promote the circular-use industry
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) will hold a ceremony to commemorate the ‘17th Resource Circulation Day’ at Gimje Indoor Gymnasium on the afternoon of September 5.
Since 2009, the Ministry has designated September 6* each year as ‘Resource Circulation Day’ to raise awareness of the need to transition to a “circular economy society” and to widely promote the importance and significance of practicing resource circulation in daily life.
* The numbers ‘9’ and ‘6’ are inverses of each other, symbolizing circulation.
This year’s Resource Circulation Day ceremony theme is “Plastic-Free, A Promise for the Earth.” It conveys the commitment, together with the public, to reduce excessive plastic use, such as disposable items, and to practice plastic-free living.
At the ceremony, government awards will be presented to contributors who have excelled in areas such as: leading resource circulation and reduction; establishing the foundation for transitioning to a circular economy society; reducing packaging materials and disposable items; exemplary use of recycled aggregates; and waste management in sectors such as food waste.
* Government Awards (Nine in total): Presidential Commendations (Two), Prime Minister’s Commendations (Seven)
Alongside the ceremony, various events will be held for public participation. The Ministry plans to promote key policies by operating citizen-participation experience booths, including activities to improve awareness and participation in waste separation, offering beverages in reusable cups for those pledging to practice plastic-free living, and exhibiting electric cleaning trucks.
In particular, this year the event will be linked with the ‘Gimje Resource Circulation Saerobomi Festival.’ From 10 a.m. on September 5, additional programs will take place at the Gimje Indoor Gymnasium parking lot and Gimje Civic Culture Cultural Park, including: exhibitions of eco-friendly products and works made from waste resources; hands-on activities making upcycled products; and education on waste separation.
On the Resource Circulation Practice Platform (recycling-info.or.kr/act4r), a campaign will continue until September 10 to encourage reducing plastic use in daily life. It includes making plastic-free pledges and submitting proof of practice.
On the same day, Minister Kim Sungwhan will also visit electric vehicle waste battery and solar panel recycling facilities located in Jeonbuk State.
The site visit was arranged to review recycling systems for future waste resources, whose volumes are expected to increase with carbon neutrality efforts and the expansion of renewable energy, and to discuss ways to promote the circular-use industry.
Minister Kim will first visit SungEel HiTech, an electric vehicle waste battery recycling company located in the Saemangeum Industrial Complex in Gunsan.
The number of waste electric vehicle batteries in Korea is expected to surge from 2,058 in 2024 to about 20,000 by 2029. From these waste batteries, key minerals for battery production, such as lithium, nickel, and cobalt, can be extracted and supplied as recycled materials. Domestic recycling companies possess internationally recognized technologies and processing systems; however, they are currently experiencing a transitional downturn due to the recent slowdown in electric vehicle market growth and the decline in global mineral prices.
The Ministry is promoting: the introduction of a certification and usage target system for recycled battery materials; the advancement of technologies for recovering key raw materials and components from waste batteries; and the recognition of cathode waste as recyclable resources. During this visit, the Minister plans to listen to on-site opinions and discuss practical support measures to help ensure the continued growth of the waste battery recycling industry.
At Seokcheong Korea, a solar panel recycling company located in Jeonju, Jeonbuk, the Minister will closely examine the recycling process of waste panels and discuss strategies to strengthen competitiveness so the industry can grow into a circular-use sector.
Since the early 2010s, solar power facilities have been installed in earnest, and as solar panels are now reaching the end of their expected lifespan, waste panels are emerging not only from power plants but also from homes, farms, and mountain areas. The volume is projected to rise sharply from 812 tons in 2024 to 9,632 tons in 2028.
To prevent illegal dumping or abandonment of waste panels and to ensure the recycling system functions smoothly, the Ministry is operating a free collection service (1599-0903) through a mutual aid association. In addition, since 2023, the Extended Producer Responsibility has been implemented for waste solar panels, and eight specialized recycling companies nationwide are participating in the circular-use industry by recovering valuable resources such as glass, aluminum, copper, and silver from waste panels.
Minister Kim Sungwhan stated, “Within this year, we will establish a ‘Plastic-Free Circular Economy Roadmap’ to build a circular economy ecosystem by fundamentally reducing disposable products and promoting eco-friendly product design.” He added, “We will actively support the future waste resource industry, which extracts key minerals from waste batteries and solar panels, so that it can become a new growth engine for local regions.”

text:
▷ Ministry of Environment launches ‘Household Waste Separation Website’ on Resource Circulation Day (September 6)
▷ Information provided on 730 items, including how and where to dispose of them in the neighborhood
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that on September 5, it will launch the Household Waste Separation and Disposal Website (분리배출.kr) to mark the 17th Resource Circulation Day (September 6 every year).
This website easily explains the separation and disposal methods for 730 types of household waste* that are mainly generated in daily life and provides guidance on the entire process of collection and processing of recyclables after separation and disposal.
* Colorless PET bottles, tumblers, mesh-patterned Styrofoam containers, paper cup ramen, milk cartons, onion nets, cold medicine, etc.
In particular, to reduce confusion caused by different separation and disposal methods in each region, it provides integrated information based on the searcher’s location, including the disposal methods and various disposal sites* in their neighborhood (city, county, or district).
* Recycling collection points, clothing collection bins, battery collection bins, fluorescent light collection bins, medicine collection bins, unmanned collection machines, etc.
By searching an item, for example, a portable battery, it will be guided to “dispose of it in a battery collection bin,” and the location of the nearest battery collection bin will be presented on a map.
In addition, this website allows users to easily find out about separation and disposal methods they have been curious about through a Q&A on waste separation and disposal.
The Household Waste Separation and Disposal Website can be accessed by directly entering the address (wasteguide.or.kr) in the internet address bar or by searching for Household Waste Separation and Disposal Website in an internet search engine.
The Ministry developed the website as a responsive web that automatically adjusts the screen size on various devices (computers, smartphones, laptops, etc.) for user convenience, and incorporated web accessibility technologies so that visually impaired users can easily use it, allowing sound to be heard when the mouse or hand hovers over text.
The Ministry plans to continuously enhance the Household Waste Separation and Disposal Website by supplementing disposal methods by city, county, district, and item. In particular, it will continuously add information requested by the public, such as searchable items and disposal sites, and improve convenience through ongoing functional enhancements*.
* Providing artificial intelligence-based object recognition services, developing a mobile app, adding voice search functionality, etc.
Kim Go-eung, Director General of Resources Circulation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, stated, “We developed a dedicated website to provide separation and disposal information easily and in detail, in line with improving public awareness of waste separation.” He added, “We will continue to provide useful information to ensure proper waste separation in the future.”

text:
▷ 53 sustainable development projects carried out in 21 Asia-Pacific countries over 20 years since 2005
▷ Over 90 participants from 29 Asia-Pacific countries share regional climate policies and strengthen climate crisis response capacity
▷ Five phase project plan (2026-2030) unveiled, serving as a green bridge linking country-specific diagnostics with follow-up projects
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that from September 8 to 9, it will jointly hold the 20th Policy Forum on Green Growth, the ‘Seoul Initiative (SINGG* or SI),’ with the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UN ESCAP) at the UN Conference Center in Bangkok, Thailand.
* Seoul Initiative Network on Green Growth
The “Seoul Initiative” was proposed by the Korean government at the 5th Ministerial Conference on Environment and Development in Asia and the Pacific, co-hosted by the Ministry of Environment and the UN ESCAP in Seoul in 2005. It was presented as a regional cooperation project to address environmental pressures resulting from economic growth in the Asia-Pacific region.
This policy forum will be held under the theme “Accelerating the Implementation of Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0*: Climate-Resilient Development in the Asia-Pacific Region,” ahead of the 10th anniversary of the Paris Agreement.
* It refers to the “2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC),” which, under the Paris Agreement, is a climate change response target that each party determines on its own to help limit global temperature rise and submits every five years. It is scheduled to be submitted to the United Nations in the second half of this year (2025).
The event, with over 90 participants from 29 countries, will feature opening remarks by: Park Yong-min, Korean Ambassador to Thailand; Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, Executive Secretary of the UN ESCAP; Jean-Claude Poimboeuf, French Ambassador to Thailand; and Phirun Saiyasitpanich, Director General at Thailand’s Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment.
The policy forum will review the implementation status of the Paris Agreement in the Asia-Pacific region and share country-specific action plans for achieving NDC 3.0 and the Paris Agreement 1.5°C target. In addition, Korea’s National Climate Change Adaptation Plan, which integrates greenhouse gas reduction and climate adaptation, will be introduced, and strategies to strengthen climate resilience through nature-based solutions will be shared, seeking an integrated approach.
In addition, to mark the 20th anniversary of the launch of the “Seoul Initiative,” the five phase project plan (2026-2030) will also be introduced.
This project plan, with the goal of “establishing the foundation for carbon neutrality and green growth,” aims to systematically support the climate crisis response capacities of Asia-Pacific countries.
First, to mainstream the climate agenda, it will be linked with major international conferences and domestic and international climate events. Network projects will expand from small-scale, single-year projects to large-scale, multi-year projects, tailored to the diverse climate-related needs of member countries.
In particular, under the five phase project plan, the network projects, which have so far focused on capacity building, will be transformed into “diagnostic projects,” where various experts participate to analyze local challenges and develop tailored solutions.
The solutions developed will be concretized* through linkage with the Ministry of Environment’s master plans for overseas expansion support, feasibility studies, and carbon neutrality and green Official Development Assistance (ODA).
* Government plan for 2026: Project-based Official Development Assistance (KRW 28 billion), etc.
Not only domestic institutions but also international organizations such as the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and multilateral development banks such as the World Bank (WB) and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) can participate in the project process, which is expected to further expand the impact of the “Seoul Initiative.”
Over the past 20 years, the “Seoul Initiative,” based on Korea’s sustainable development experience, has provided about KRW 10.1 billion to support policy consultation, knowledge sharing, and capacity building, while carrying out 19 policy forums and 53 network projects across 21 countries. This year, projects such as the “Capacity Building for Local Government Greenhouse Gas Reduction” in the Philippines and the “Capacity Building for Waste-to-Energy Systems” in Fiji are also underway.
Jeong Eun-hae, Director General of International Cooperation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, stated, “The Seoul Initiative has been a hub of environmental cooperation driving sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific region over the past 20 years.” She added, “Through the five phase project plan, we will actively serve as a green bridge linking country-specific diagnostics with follow-up projects, thereby generating tangible climate action and green transition outcomes in the Asia-Pacific region.”

text:
▷ Business agreement between Ministry of Environment, textile and fabric industry, cement industry, and Korea Recycling Service Agency
▷ Separated and sorted waste fabric scraps turned into yarn, fabric, and clothing products; intermediate processed fuel used for thermal recycling
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that on September 9, it will sign a business agreement for a pilot project to establish a recycling system for waste fabric scraps generated from sewing factories, with the textile, fabric, and cement industries as well as textile-related associations*, at the Ministry annex conference room in Eojin-dong, Sejong.
* Pang Rim, Sewang, Sinhan Spinning & Textile, Ssangyong C&E, Asia Cement, Korea Recycling Service Agency (KORA)
Prior to this agreement, in January last year (2024), the Ministry signed a business agreement with four basic local governments in Seoul (Jongno-gu, Dongdaemun-gu, Seongdong-gu, and Dobong-gu) and the KORA, and has been conducting a pilot project to shift waste fabric scraps to a material-recycling-centered system. Through the pilot project, waste fabric scraps that had been incinerated or landfilled are now being separated by material, sorted, and recycled into products such as shoe midsoles, automotive sound-absorbing materials, and thermal covers.
The pilot project under this agreement aims to expand the scope of recycling from the existing agreement. Cotton will be produced from the separated and sorted waste fabric scraps and used as raw material for yarn, fabric, and clothing products. Intermediate processed fuel, selected and processed to specific standards and materials, will be used as fuel by cement companies.
The KORA, which participated in this agreement, plans to cooperate in ensuring smooth supply of raw materials and recycling to its member companies and agreement participants through the separation and sorting of waste fabric scraps.
The textile and fabric industry will support the use of textile and fabric raw materials produced through sorting and processing, as well as the export and sale of the finished products, while the cement industry will actively support the smooth handling of the sorted and recycled intermediate fabric-derived fuel.
The Ministry will oversee and implement this pilot project, providing administrative support and institutional improvements to ensure the smooth execution of waste fabric scrap separation, collection, and recycling systems. In addition, it plans to continuously evaluate the recycling performance of waste fabric scraps and reflect the results in policy.
Kim Go-eung, Director General of Resources Circulation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, stated, “The separation, sorting, and recycling of waste are essential elements for producing high-quality recycled raw materials.” He added, “To establish a circular system, we will continue to identify and expand various measures so that the supply of excellent recycled raw materials and the securing of demand sources can be balanced.”

▷ National Institute of Environmental Research holds the 7th Cheollian satellite 2 convergence utilization conference
The National Institute of Environmental Research (NIER) under the Ministry of Environment announced that it will hold the “7th Cheollian Satellite 2 (2A/2B)* Convergence Utilization Conference” jointly with the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (KHOA, Director General Jung Kyu-sam), the National Meteorological Satellite Center (NMSC, Director Kim Yoon-jae), and the Korea Institute of Ocean Science & Technology (KIOST, President Lee Hyi Seung), which are participating organizations of the Cheollian Satellite 2 Convergence Utilization Council. The conference will be held for two days starting September 11 at H Hotel Sejong City (located in Heungdeok-gu, Cheongju).
* Cheollian-2A: Meteorological satellite launched in 2018; Cheollian-2B: Ocean and environment satellite launched in 2020
Marking its 7th year, this conference has been held annually since 2019. It serves as a venue for inter-agency cooperation, where organizations involved in the development and operation of the Cheollian satellite 2 gather to discuss strengthening the use of satellite data in the fields of meteorology, oceanography, and environment.
At this conference, experts from related institutions and academia will attend to promote mutual cooperation in the areas of data sharing, convergence information production, and service improvement, in order to enhance the operation, quality management, and expanded convergence utilization of the Cheollian satellite 2.
On the first day of the conference, a special lecture will feature Kim Eung-Hyun, Director of Satellite Mission Design Program at the Korea Aerospace Administration (KASA), presenting on the satellite promotion strategy of the KASA; Han Dong-hoon, Director of National Spatial Data Infrastructure Center at the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, presenting on the current status and plans for operating the National Spatial Data Infrastructure Platform; and Kim Pil-sung, Deputy Minister of the Disaster Information Research Division at the National Disaster Management Research Institute of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, presenting on the current status and plans for satellite utilization in the disaster field.
In the following lectures, participating organizations will give expert presentations on the themes of current status and plans for the convergence utilization of the Cheollian satellite 2, research on calibration and quality management, and joint research in meteorology, oceanography, and environment.
On the second day, separate sessions will be held on convergence utilization of geostationary satellites, data exchange, and practical meetings on quality management. These will focus on discussing cooperation measures for the joint development of organizations involved in the development and operation of the Cheollian satellites through expanded convergence utilization and the sharing of data quality management technologies.
In particular, the NIER Environmental Satellite Center will share the current status and plans for the use of the Geostationary Environment Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS) and present the results of medium- to long-term analyses of sensor observation data for stable mission performance checks, as well as the status of preprocessing data verification.
Seong Ji-won, Director General of the Atmospheric Environmental Research Department at the National Institute of Environmental Research, stated, “Through this conference, we will strengthen cooperation among organizations operating the Cheollian satellite 2 and provide diverse satellite information through convergence utilization.” She added, “We will also ensure thorough preparation for the development of follow-up environmental satellites to secure continuity in satellite-based air pollutant observation data.”

text:
▷ Ministry of Environment to hold a public hearing on September 12 to prepare the draft national emission allowances allocation plan for the 4th commitment period (2026-2030)
▷ To gather opinions from diverse stakeholders including industry and civil society, it will be livestreamed on the ministry’s YouTube channel, with an online public hearing to be held in parallel
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) will hold a public hearing to gather broad opinions on the “National Emission Allowances Allocation Plan (Draft) for the 4th Commitment Period (2026-2030)” on September 12 at 2 p.m. at the Korea Finance for Construction (KFINCO)* (4th floor, main conference room).
* 15 Boramae-ro 5-gil, Dongjak-gu, Seoul (Sindaebang-dong, KFINCO)
Considering the heightened public interest in the Emissions Trading Scheme, which is a key component of the national greenhouse gas reduction policy, this public hearing will be broadcast live on the Ministry of Environment’s YouTube channel* in addition to in-person participation. An online public hearing through e-People will also be held from September 12 to 15.
* Participation is available through the Ministry of Environment LIVE YouTube channel (http://www.youtube.com/mevnewsroom).
At the public hearing, the draft of the 4th Allocation Plan, which presents comprehensive standards for greenhouse gas emission allowances allocation over the 5-year 4th commitment period, and the draft amendment to the 3rd Allocation Plan, aimed at correcting the overallocation* in the power generation sector during the 3rd commitment period, will be announced. A public discussion with participation from academia, industry, civil society, and experts will follow to exchange a wide range of opinions.
* Due to the omission of energy statistics (coal consumption by private power generation companies), national greenhouse gas emissions from 2016 to 2022 were underestimated, resulting in an overallocation of the total emission allowances for the general power generation sector (49 companies) during the 3rd commitment period.
In the 4th commitment period, more than 700 companies that meet or exceed the legal threshold* will participate in the Emissions Trading Scheme. Under the 4th Master Plan for the Emissions Trading Scheme (2026-2035), the allocation targets will be classified into two sectors: power generation and non-power generation.
* Companies with an average annual emissions of 125,000 tons of CO2-eq or more during the baseline years (2022-2024), or those that own a facility with annual emissions of 25,000 tons of CO2-eq or more.
The total emission allowances will be set to address the surplus allowances and price decline issues from the 3rd commitment period, while also encouraging companies to invest in greenhouse gas reduction. The reserve for market stabilization, incorporated within the total emission allowances under the 4th Master Plan, will be calculated by comprehensively considering corporate burdens and the potential for future economic fluctuations.
Paid allocation will be expanded and differentiated between the power generation sector and the non-power generation sector in accordance with the 4th Master Plan. However, industries at risk of carbon leakage, such as the steel and petrochemicals industries, which account for most high greenhouse gas-emitting sectors, as well as institutions serving the public interest, will continue to receive free allocations as in the 3rd commitment period.
The Ministry of Environment will review and incorporate the opinions presented at this public hearing to finalize the “National Emission Allowances Allocation Plan (Draft) for the 4th Commitment Period (2026-2030).” The plan will then go through deliberation by the Allocation Committee (chaired by the Minister of Economy and Finance), the Presidential Commission on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth, and the Cabinet Council, and is scheduled to be finalized within the second half of this year.
Opinions on the draft of the 4th Allocation Plan can be submitted either through real-time comments on the online channel during the public hearing or via email (werb12@korea.kr) within three days, by September 15.
Oh Il-young, Director General for Climate Change and International Cooperation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, stated, “The 4th commitment period is a critical time that will determine whether Korea achieves its 2030 NDC in the international community.” He added, “We will thoroughly review the opinions raised at this public hearing and establish a plan that reflects the current status of companies and the specific characteristics of each industry to efficiently achieve the NDC.”

▷ Sharing the current status and discussing future plans of the two countries’ international greenhouse gas mitigation projects
▷ Discussing and adopting draft detailed implementation rules to accelerate the implementation of Korea-Kazakhstan international mitigation projects
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) will hold the “1st Korea-Kazakhstan Joint Committee on Cooperation for Implementing Article 6 of the Paris Agreement” in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, on September 12 to expand bilateral cooperation on international greenhouse gas mitigation projects.
The Joint Committee will be attended by Jeong Eun-hae, Director General of International Cooperation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, and Saule Sabieva, Director of the Climate Policy Department of Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, as well as officials* from both governments and institutions related to international greenhouse gas mitigation projects.
* Composition of the 1st Korea-Kazakhstan Joint Committee: (Korean side) Ministry of Environment, Korea Environment Corporation, etc.
(Kazakhstan side) Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Industry and Construction, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Environmental Corporation, etc.
This Joint Committee is the first meeting held under the “Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation for Article 6 of the Paris Agreement between Korea and Kazakhstan,” signed in June last year (2024) by Korea’s Ministry of Environment and Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources.
At this meeting, the two countries will share their respective policies for implementing Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and discuss the current progress and future plans of the international greenhouse gas mitigation projects they are pursuing.
Currently, the Ministry of Environment is promoting two international greenhouse gas mitigation projects* in Kazakhstan, which involve capturing methane generated from two landfills, incinerating it, and linking it to power generation.
* 1) Karasai Landfill Gas Incineration/Power Generation Project; 2) Aktobe Landfill Gas Incineration/Power Generation Project
Through this Joint Committee, the two countries are expected to build a consensus that international greenhouse gas mitigation projects based on Article 6 of the Paris Agreement will contribute to achieving both nations’ Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), as well as to addressing Kazakhstan’s environmental issues and promoting sustainable development.
In addition, the two countries plan to seek ways of cooperation to promptly advance the two international greenhouse gas mitigation projects currently being promoted by the Ministry of Environment, including the Karasai Landfill Gas Incineration and Power Generation Project in Kazakhstan.
Meanwhile, at this Joint Committee, the two countries will discuss the draft detailed implementation rules, including the procedures for carrying out international greenhouse gas mitigation projects and the operation of the Joint Committee. These rules are expected to be adopted through follow-up consultations. Once adopted, they are anticipated to lay the foundation for accelerating the implementation of international greenhouse gas mitigation projects between the two countries.
Jeong Eun-hae, Director General of International Cooperation Bureau, stated, “Taking this 1st Joint Committee as an opportunity, we will strengthen support to both help address Kazakhstan’s climate and environmental issues and promote sustainable development through international greenhouse gas mitigation projects, while also enabling Korean climate and environment companies to expand their entry into the Kazakhstani market.”

text:
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that, following the ation of the new government’s 123 national policy tasks at the Cabinet meeting on September 16, it will faithfully implement five climate and environment policy tasks, including achieving carbon neutrality and establishing a circular economy ecosystem.
The main details of the climate and environment policy tasks are as follows.
First, carbon neutrality will be achieved for a sustainable future.
An implementation strategy will be established to ensure the achievement of the 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and within this year a more advanced 2035 NDC compared to the 2030 goal will also be set, along with a long-term mitigation roadmap for carbon neutrality through 2050. In addition, the government will strengthen the carbon competitiveness of domestic industries through measures such as enacting the Carbon Neutral Industry Act and expanding green public procurement, while supporting the accelerated transition from internal combustion engine vehicles to electric vehicles. Public participation will be expanded through enhanced incentives under the Carbon Neutral Points System, and Korea’s global leadership in climate and environment will be reinforced by creating K-initiatives in the climate and environment field.
The second task is to establish a circular economy ecosystem.
Through a public deliberation process, a national roadmap for a plastic-free circular economy will be established within this year. Circular resource use will be enhanced by introducing sustainable product design such as Korean-style eco-design and building category-specific recycling systems for items such as waste batteries. In addition, the competitiveness of circular economy companies will be strengthened by supporting and encouraging participation of leading circular economy enterprises and industrial complexes, and by operating regulatory sandboxes for new technologies. Furthermore, leading circular economy projects will be expanded, including the heat link initiative that supplies waste incineration heat to industrial complexes.
The third task is to strengthen the nation’s climate adaptation capacity.
A command center for national climate response will be established by building an integrated platform for climate adaptation information and formulating the Fourth National Climate Change Adaptation Plan within this year. In addition, the climate risk resilience of national infrastructure will be enhanced based on advanced climate change monitoring and forecasting, as well as comprehensive socio-economic climate impact assessments. Climate response capacity will also be strengthened across all sectors of society and the economy through industry support and the protection of vulnerable groups.
The fourth task is to create a pleasant environment that everyone can enjoy.
Management of fine dust emission sources will be strengthened across all sectors including workplaces, transportation, and daily life. Harmful algal bloom damage will be prevented through stable water supply, the establishment of new toxin standards for algal blooms, improvement of response systems, and tighter management of pollution sources. In addition, safety management of hazardous chemicals and products will be reinforced, while the effectiveness of measures for preventing environmental damage and providing remedies will be enhanced to better protect public health.
The fifth task is to restore the natural state of the four major rivers and the biodiversity of the Korean Peninsula.
The weirs of the four major rivers will be opened according to the conditions of each facility, and improvement projects for water intake and pumping stations will be carried out promptly. In addition to creating healthy rivers, systematic conservation of the national territory and restoration of biodiversity will be promoted by designating 30 percent of the land as protected areas by 2030, restoring degraded ecosystems, and revitalizing eco-tourism, thereby enhancing the quality of ecosystem services enjoyed by the public.
Vice Minister of Environment Kum Hanseung stated, “In implementing the national policy tasks, we will strengthen public participation and communication in line with a people-centered government, and spare no effort in delivering results that the public can genuinely experience.”

▷ International event (Green Cooperation Forum) held to support overseas expansion of environmental companies
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) and the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute announced that they will hold the 4th “Korea?Multilateral Development Bank (MDB) Green Cooperation Forum” on September 18 at The Westin Seoul Parnas Hotel (located in Gangnam-gu, Seoul).
Since 2022, the Ministry of Environment has been hosting the “Green Cooperation Forum,” an international event that facilitates meetings between multilateral development banks and domestic companies, in order to support overseas expansion of Korean environmental companies together with its affiliated agency, the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute (KEITI).
This year’s event will focus on “The Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Climate and Environment Sector” and plans to share the AI strategies of Korean companies (such as water management, waste recycling, and flood forecasting) with multilateral development banks that are pursuing new climate and environment projects using AI technology.
A multilateral development bank is an international financial institution established with joint capital contributions from multiple countries. It provides funding to promote sustainable development in developing countries and is one of the sources that Korean companies can utilize for their overseas expansion.
On this day, major multilateral development banks such as the World Bank (WB), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the African Development Bank (AfDB), and the Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI) will participate and present on “Mid- to Long-term Strategies for Utilizing Artificial Intelligence and Opportunities for New Projects.”
The KEITI, the Export-Import Bank of Korea, and other Korean public institutions will introduce cases of cooperation with multilateral development banks, with the aim of supporting domestic climate and environment companies that possess AI-based green technologies in fields such as water management, waste management, and flood response to participate in new projects promoted by the multilateral development banks.
In addition, starting with this event, a “Networking Session” will be arranged to facilitate one-on-one meetings between domestic environmental companies and multilateral development banks, helping them establish cooperative projects together.
Meanwhile, this year the Ministry of Environment is carrying out preliminary feasibility studies with multilateral development banks, including an AI-based urban waste resource circulation project in Colombia, an integrated air quality management project in Jakarta, Indonesia, a compressed biogas development project in Maharashtra, India, and a waste oil recycling project in Abidjan, C?te d’Ivoire.
Jeong Eun-hae, Director General of International Cooperation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, stated, “Artificial intelligence is already a core technology for energy transition and climate crisis response in the international community.” She added, “We will further strengthen cooperation with multilateral development banks to lead the global green transition and faithfully serve as a bridge to help our companies thrive on the world stage.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Ministry of Environment, Korea Environment Corporation, and Korea Auto Dismantlement Recycling Association sign business agreement to support distribution of used EV batteries from small scrapyards, including storage, evaluation, and sales
▷ Domestic circulation and utilization of used batteries containing large amounts of critical minerals expected to be promoted 
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that on September 23, at the Metropolitan Future Waste Resources Base Collection Center* (located in Siheung, Gyeonggi-do), it will sign a “Business Agreement for Supporting the Distribution of Used Batteries Not Subject to Mandatory Return” together with the Korea Environment Corporation and the Korea Auto Dismantlement Recycling Association (KADRA).
* A facility established and operated by the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation to support a full-cycle resource circulation system, including the collection, storage, and sale of future waste resources such as electric vehicle batteries and solar panels (Installation and operation of the Future Waste Resources Collection Center under Article 20-4 of the Act on Resource Circulation of Electrical and Electronic Equipment and Vehicles).
Currently, the obligation to return and the processing procedures for electric vehicle batteries at the time of scrapping differ depending on the year the vehicle was purchased.
Electric vehicles that received purchase subsidies before 2021 must return their batteries to the national or local government after use. The returned batteries are then evaluated for performance at the Future Waste Resources Base Collection Center and subsequently sold for reuse or recycling purposes.
For vehicles that received purchase subsidies after 2021, there is no obligation to return the battery. Once removed at scrapyards, the batteries are freely traded in the private market.
However, most scrapyards lack the necessary infrastructure, such as storage facilities for used electric vehicle batteries, performance evaluation equipment, and sales systems. As a result, removed batteries are often left unattended for long periods, and without the ability to independently assess their residual value, they are not being utilized as high-value resources such as for reuse.
Accordingly, through this agreement, the Ministry of Environment will promote a pilot project for the safe and efficient distribution of electric vehicle batteries not subject to mandatory return until a private autonomous distribution system for used batteries is established.
The Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation will provide administrative and institutional support for the operation of the pilot project, and using four Future Waste Resources Base Collection Centers nationwide*, will handle the receipt, performance evaluation, storage, and sale of batteries on behalf of stakeholders.
* Seoul Metropolitan Area (Siheung, Gyeonggi-do), Yeongnam Region (Dalseo-gu, Daegu), Honam Region (Jeongeup, Jeollabuk-do), Chungcheong Region (Hongseong, Chungcheongnam-do)
The KADRA will be responsible for operating a cooperative platform to provide information on the generation and collection of used batteries between scrapyards and the Korea Environment Corporation.
In addition, for this year’s pilot project, the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation will exempt scrapyards from the service fees* they would normally have to pay to the base collection centers, in order to encourage their participation.
* It currently costs about KRW 640,000 per used electric vehicle battery for labor, equipment, and storage required for performance evaluation.
Scrapyards will be able to reduce the burden of facility investment caused by electric vehicle dismantling and quickly distribute used batteries.
This agreement is a follow-up measure to the “Battery Recycling Promotion Plan” announced by the government on May 14 of this year. It aims to supplement the lack of distribution infrastructure at scrapyards with public facilities, thereby ensuring that used batteries not subject to mandatory return can be reused and recycled domestically.
Through this, a foundation is expected to be established for the recycling of key minerals such as lithium and nickel.
Kim Go-eung, Director General of the Resource Circulation Bureau at the Ministry of Environment, stated, “This business agreement will serve as an important starting point for establishing a stable and rapid distribution system for used batteries through public-private cooperation.” He added, “We will actively promote the domestic circulation and utilization of electric vehicle batteries to secure a stable supply chain of recyclable resources.”

text:
▷ Completion of Korea’s first renewable energy complex, the “Imha Dam Floating Solar Power Project”
▷ Maximizing resident income through the sunshine pension and strengthening renewable energy management for carbon neutrality through wind power site inspections
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that Vice Minister Kum Hanseung will attend the completion ceremony of the “Imha Dam Floating Solar Power Project,” to be held on September 25 at Imha Multi-purpose Dam Park in Andong, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and will subsequently visit the GS Wind Power Complex site in Yeongyang, Gyeongsangbuk-do.
At the completion ceremony held that morning, Vice Minister Kum Hanseung, Andong Mayor Kwon Gichang, Korea Water Resources Corporation CEO Yun Seogdae, and other officials shared the achievements of Korea’s first renewable energy complex, which was realized through cooperation between the local government and residents.
The “Imha Dam Floating Solar Power Project” has a total capacity of 47.2MW and was built utilizing the water surface of the dam in the Imdong-myeon and Imha-myeon areas of Andong, Gyeongsangbuk-do. Led by the city of Andong, with local residents (33 villages in Imdong-myeon and Imha-myeon) participating as investors, it was designated in 2021 as Korea’s first renewable energy complex*.
* A system in which local governments take the lead in systematically establishing renewable energy generation facilities with a capacity exceeding 40MW
The Imha Dam Floating Solar Power Complex is a leading example that combines energy production with regional coexistence, while also maximizing resident benefits. About 2,700 households in Andong will receive an average annual “sunshine pension” worth around KRW 400,000 (in goods and cash), consisting of resident participation profits and additional income from the complex designation, for 20 years after power generation begins.
In addition, although there were concerns about delays due to limited grid capacity, the project was able to begin commercial operation early, on July 30 of this year (2025), by introducing Korea’s first “cross-generation” system. This method utilizes the existing transmission lines of the Imha Dam hydropower plant, operating floating solar power during the day and hydropower at night.
At the completion ceremony, the Ministry will also proclaim the transition toward a decarbonized green civilization centered on renewable energy. The Imha Dam Floating Solar Power Project is expected to produce 61,670MWh of clean energy annually, supplying electricity to about 25% (20,000 households) of all households in Andong, while achieving an annual greenhouse gas reduction of approximately 28,000 tons.
Meanwhile, in the afternoon, Vice Minister Kum will visit the GS Wind Power Complex to inspect major facilities, including access and management roads, and to hear from officials about the operation status of the wind farm, emergency response systems, and strategies for coexistence with local residents.
The GS Wind Power Complex is also an example of returning generation profits to local residents, carrying out various support initiatives such as scholarship programs within the region, hosting the GS Wind Power Cup soccer tournament, and providing health check-up support.
Vice Minister Kum stated, “Expanding renewable energy is a key task in responding to the climate crisis, and it is essential to balance environmental performance with local community acceptance. Going forward, we will continue to pursue carbon neutrality centered on renewable energy, based on coexistence with local communities, and actively respond to the era of climate crisis.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Revitalizing Korea-Philippines biodiversity research and strengthening cooperation
The National Institute of Biological Resources (NIBR, President Yoo Ho) under the Ministry of Environment announced that it will hold an opening ceremony for the biological specimen room in Puerto Princesa, Palawan* Province, Philippines, on September 25.
* Palawan consists of more than 1,700 islands, has a relatively low population density, with 50% of its primary forests preserved, and is rich in biodiversity, home to over 200 endemic species.
In June 2018, the NIBR signed a “Memorandum of Understanding on Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Use” with the Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources, and since then has been conducting biodiversity-related research in Palawan on plants, insects, amphibians and reptiles, fungi, and more.
The opening of the biological specimen room in Palawan, Philippines, is based on the “Agreement on the Establishment of a Biological Specimen Room in the Philippines” signed in March of this year (2025) between the NIBR and Puerto Princesa City, Palawan Province, to lay the foundation for local biodiversity conservation and further strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
The NIBR will provide internationally standardized sealed specimen storage facilities, along with equipment such as dehumidifiers and air conditioners to maintain temperature and humidity, in the site and building prepared by the Philippine side.
At the opening ceremony, representatives from four institutions - the Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Puerto Princesa City of Palawan, the Palawan Council for Sustainable Development, and the University of the Philippines Los Banos - as well as local residents will attend to express their interest in and appreciation for the opening of the biological specimen room.
In addition, the NIBR will donate about 300 copies of a biodiversity field guide containing information on 298 species of birds, amphibians and reptiles, fish, insects, plants, and fungi from the Palawan region, jointly researched with the Philippines, to the Philippine Department of Environment and Natural Resources. The donated guides will later be used for Palawan biodiversity research by Philippine government agencies, research institutions, and universities.
Meanwhile, through the “Biodiversity Capacity-Building Project” being carried out with the Philippines since 2019, the NIBR has so far trained eight local researchers, including government officials involved in biodiversity policy and university personnel.
They are expected to serve as a bridge in continuing cooperation between the two countries, including joint biodiversity research in the Philippines and the operation of the biological specimen room.
President Yoo Ho stated, “In order to conserve global biodiversity and implement the UN’s ‘Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF)*,’ we must strengthen international cooperation and support for biodiversity.” She added, “We will further expand joint biodiversity research with other Southeast Asian countries as well.”
* Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework action goals: financial support for biodiversity conservation in developing countries (over USD 30 billion by 2030), biodiversity capacity building, promotion of technology transfer, and scientific and technological cooperation.

text:
▷ The 26th Tripartite Environment Ministers Meeting successfully held in Yantai, China, September 27-28
▷ Expanded cooperation in climate, plastics, and living environment, with various side events such as the youth forum
▷ 20th anniversary commemorative event of Korea-Shandong environmental cooperation held and memorandum of understanding signed
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that the “26th Tripartite Environment Ministers Meeting (TEMM26),” held in Yantai, Shandong Province, China, from September 27 to 28 with the participation of Korea, China, and Japan, concluded successfully.
The meeting was attended by Kim Sungwhan, Minister of Environment of Korea; Huang Runqiu, Minister of Ecology and Environment of China; and Asao Keiichiro, Minister of the Environment of Japan. Through bilateral talks, the plenary session, a joint press conference, and various side events, the three ministers shared the achievements of environmental cooperation in Northeast Asia and discussed future directions for collaboration.
At the plenary session, Minister Kim stated, “With the launch of the new government, the Republic of Korea has adopted climate crisis response and sustainable energy transition as its national environmental strategy. To support this, the ‘Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment,’ which integrates the functions of climate, energy, and environment, will be launched in early October.” He emphasized that this will serve as a foundation to maximize policy synergy and accelerate the transition from a carbon-based civilization to a green civilization.
In response, Minister Huang Runqiu and Minister Asao Keiichiro congratulated Korea on its organizational restructuring and expressed their hopes for the seamless implementation of its carbon neutrality policy.
In particular, at this meeting, the three countries agreed to take the TEMM, which had previously focused on environmental policy cooperation such as improving air quality and conserving biodiversity, to the next level by significantly strengthening cooperation in the field of climate going forward.
Minister Kim emphasized, “Korea, China, and Japan together account for more than one-third of global greenhouse gas emissions, and cooperation among the three countries on climate response will play an important role in achieving global carbon neutrality.” To this end, the three countries discussed major climate issues such as the “2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)” and agreed to begin holding regular climate policy dialogues starting in 2026, as well as to strengthen cooperation on carbon markets and carbon labeling.
At the bilateral meeting between Korea and China held prior to the main conference, the two sides shared the achievements of the Blue Sky Plan in improving air quality and agreed to strengthen cooperation on global environmental issues such as responding to the climate crisis and plastic pollution, with a focus on the Korea-China Environmental Cooperation Center.
At the Korea-Japan bilateral meeting, Korea shared its experience with the carbon market in relation to Japan’s Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS), which will be implemented next year, and the two sides discussed cooperation in the field of biodiversity, including responses to invasive species and the protection of internationally endangered species.
In addition to the plenary session, various side events were held during the meeting, further broadening the scope of cooperation.
Minister Kim met with five Korean youth representatives attending the Youth Forum and shared views with them, saying, “When you look at the Earth from space, there are no borders, only clouds, seas, and land. Therefore, pollutants emitted from each country require a joint response, and for this, the cooperation of future generations is more important than anything else.”
He added, “We hope that the decarbonization efforts of the youth in Korea, China, and Japan will expand beyond Northeast Asia into global cooperation.”
At the “10th Tripartite Roundtable on Environmental Business,” government officials, industry representatives, and experts participated to discuss “ways to achieve carbon neutrality.”
Lee Oksu, Head of the Sustainability & Climate Center at Kim & Chang Law Firm, presented plans for promoting green finance based on the Korean Green Taxonomy. He stressed, “The global flow of finance will determine the success or failure of the carbon neutrality transition,” and added, “We must systematically support domestic companies’ investment demand for green transition through the revision of the Korean Green Taxonomy and the introduction of transition finance guidelines.”
In his closing remarks, Minister Kim stated, “Korea, China, and Japan have overcome past challenges together through environmental cooperation, and now we have pledged new actions in the face of the civilizational task of the climate crisis.” He added, “We hope that today’s agreements and commitments will serve as a foundation for leading the green transition not only in Northeast Asia but also across the world.”
Meanwhile, at the commemorative event for the 20th anniversary of Korea-Shandong environmental cooperation held during the TEMM, Minister Kim stated, “Over the past 20 years, based on unwavering trust and friendship, we have achieved tangible results in areas such as air quality improvement, environmental business exchanges, and technological cooperation,” expressing gratitude to the Shandong provincial government for its efforts. He emphasized, “Humanity is now facing the civilizational challenge of the climate crisis, and we must move beyond the limits of industrial civilization to transition into a decarbonization-based green civilization.”
The Ministry of Environment announced that, taking the TEMM and the 20th anniversary of Korea-Shandong environmental cooperation as an opportunity, it plans to further deepen trilateral cooperation and pursue concrete actions for responding to the climate crisis and advancing the green transition.

text:
▷ Nakdonggang National Institute of Biological Resources analyzes the distribution of 28 endangered wild fish species under a greenhouse gas emission scenario with rising average temperatures
The Nakdonggang National Institute of Biological Resources (NNIBR, President Yong Seok-won) under the Ministry of Environment announced that if the greenhouse gas emission scenario, which projects an average temperature rise of 4.2℃ by 2080, is actually applied, 19 out of 28 fish species designated as endangered wildlife could disappear.
The 28 endangered wild fish species analyzed this time consist of 11 Class I species and 17 Class II species.
* A total of 29 endangered wild fish species have been designated, including 19 endemic species, but the black star fat minnow (Endangered Wildlife Class II) was excluded from this analysis due to a lack of distribution data.
The analysis showed that under the climate change scenario in which the average temperature rises by 4.2℃ by 2080, 19 of these fish species are expected to disappear.
The 19 species are: Buan spine loach, Hangang bitterling, slender shinner, Chinese nine spine stickleback, black shinner, aucha perch, cat’s eye eightbarbel gudgeon, short eightbarbel gudgeon, yellow fin sculpin, Korean bitterling, Miho spine loach, Tachanovsky’s gudgeon, spotted barbel, Eurasian minnow, Manchurian lenok, large striped bitterling, bullhead torrent catfish, Tumen river sculpin, and white eightbarbel gudgeon. Among these, 13 species*, including the Buan spine loach, are endemic to Korea and found nowhere else.
* Buan spine loach, Hangang bitterling, slender shinner, black shinner, cat’s eye eightbarbel gudgeon, short eightbarbel gudgeon, yellow fin sculpin, Korean bitterling, Miho spine loach, spotted barbel, large striped bitterling, bullhead torrent catfish, white eightbarbel gudgeon
The research team at the NNIBR used biodiversity survey data accumulated by the National Institute of Environmental Research, the Korea National Park Service, and the National Institute of Ecology, as well as the “National Climate Change Standard Scenario” provided by the Korea Meteorological Administration and the National Spatial Information Platform, for this analysis.
The ‘National Climate Change Standard Scenario’ incorporates the ‘high-carbon emission scenario (SSP5)*’ presented by the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) in August 2021.
* A scenario in which the use of fossil fuels and reckless development focused solely on economic growth leads to a rapid increase in greenhouse gas emissions
The ‘high-carbon emission scenario (SSP5)’ projects that by 2080, global greenhouse gas emissions will reach about 129.5 gigatons (GtCO2), more than three times the 2023 level of 37.8 gigatons (GtCO2). If this scenario unfolds, the average temperature in Korea will rise by about 4.2℃.
The research team predicted that under this scenario, the Chinese nine spine stickleback, Buan spine loach, and Hangang bitterling would be the first to disappear by 2050. And by 2080, the range of extinctions would expand to include species such as the white eightbarbel gudgeon, Manchurian lenok, and spotted barbel.
In contrast, if the ‘low-carbon emission scenario (SSP1)*’ unfolds, global greenhouse gas emissions are projected to decrease to about 33.4 gigatons (GtCO2) by 2080, and 93% (26 species) of the endangered wild fish analyzed in this study are expected to survive even in 2080.
* A scenario aimed at sustainable and eco-friendly growth, in which greenhouse gas emissions are significantly reduced.
Ryu Si-hyun, Deputy Minister of the Biodiversity Research Team at the NNIBR, stated, “This study scientifically analyzed the impact of climate change on biological species by utilizing national public data collected long-term by various institutions.”

title: Press Release

▷ First public bear protection facility opens in Korea, providing care for ten bears purchased by civic organizations
The Ministry of Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that the public bear protection facility, jointly established with Gurye County in Masan-myeon, Gurye-gun, Jeollanam-do, will open on September 30 and begin caring for ten captive bears purchased by civic organizations from related farms.
The opening ceremony, to be held in the afternoon, will be attended by Vice Minister of Environment Kum Hanseung, National Assembly Deputy Speaker Lee Hack-young, Gurye County Governor Kim Sun-ho, Korea National Park Service Director Joo Dae-young, and Korean Animal Welfare Association Director Cho Hee-kyung.
The “Gurye Bear Protection Facility” was established near Jirisan National Park in Masan-myeon, Gurye County, on a site covering a total area of 25,744 square meters after Gurye County was selected in February 2021 for a national subsidy project. The facility consists of three outdoor enclosures, two breeding buildings, and one quarantine building, and is designed to accommodate and protect up to 49 bears.
Gurye County, which manages the facility, has established a consignment operation system with the Korea National Park Service, an organization with expertise in managing wild animals such as bears, and has completed preparations to protect the captive bears.
Meanwhile, the ten bears transferred to the facility were purchased by civic organizations from a farm in Yeoncheon County, Gyeonggi Province, in accordance with the “Agreement on Ending Bear Farming,” signed in January 2022 between the Ministry of Environment, local governments, bear farmers, and civic groups such as Korean Animal Welfare Association and Green Korea.
However, some of these bears have sustained injuries, such as missing limbs or damage to their teeth or eyesight. These individuals are expected to recover their health through further examinations and treatment by veterinarians and other specialists.
At the opening ceremony, Vice Minister Kum Hanseung will exchange views with officials from Gurye County, the Korea National Park Service, and civic organizations on the current status and future direction of ending bear farming, and will discuss ways to cooperate with stakeholders to ensure the stable operation of the protection facility.
Vice Minister of Environment Kum Hanseung stated, “The opening of the Gurye Bear Protection Facility is a result of cooperation achieved through the joint efforts of the government, the National Assembly, and civil society.” He added, “The Ministry of Environment will continue to work tirelessly to end bear farming by promoting support projects to protect the remaining captive bears.”

▷ Governments, civil society, and businesses from around the world gather in Abu Dhabi to explore ways to conserve nature
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that it will participate in the “2025 International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) World Conservation Congress (WCC)” to be held in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE), from October 9 to 15.
The IUCN is the world’s largest international organization dedicated to conserving resources and nature, established in 1948 with the support of the United Nations. It has over 1,400 member organizations from more than 170 countries and more than 18,000 experts actively involved. The IUCN contributes to global biodiversity conservation, including evaluating sites for inscription as UNESCO World Natural Heritage sites.
This WCC is the largest international conference for discussing nature conservation and sustainable development, and South Korea previously hosted the Congress in Jeju in 2012.
The WCC consists of three main parts: the Members’ Assembly, the pre-conference forum, and the exhibition events. The Members’ Assembly, held from October 13 to 15, serves as the IUCN’s highest decision-making body, where all member organizations gather to discuss operational matters such as the IUCN’s work plan for 2026-2029 and to vote on motions submitted by members concerning nature conservation.
At this WCC, the MCEE will participate as a national member representing South Korea, actively engaging not only in discussions on the future operational direction of the IUCN but also in key decisions related to nature conservation, such as motions on biodiversity credits* and synthetic biology**.
* A system that allows the ecological impacts resulting from biodiversity protection and restoration activities or corporate operations to be converted into monetary value and traded
** A field of biotechnology that involves the engineering, design, creation, and application of the components and systems of living organisms
The pre-conference forum, held from October 9 to 12 prior to the Members’ Assembly, will feature presentations, discussions, and lectures on various topics, providing a platform to share knowledge on nature conservation and sustainable development across a wide range of fields, including economics, society, and science and technology.
The National Institute of Ecology, an affiliated organization of the MCEE, will present, together with POSCO, South Korea’s public-private cooperation efforts in response to natural capital disclosure* at the forum on October 11.
* A system that discloses to investors information on a company’s natural capital by incorporating related indicators into its financial statements
From October 9 to 13, the MCEE will operate a promotional booth showcasing South Korea’s carbon neutrality policies, such as the Emissions Trading System (ETS), as well as nature conservation initiatives like the restoration of endangered species and policies supporting the transition to a circular economy. In addition, a side event will be held to present the outcomes of projects aimed at strengthening capacity for natural capital disclosure, conducted in cooperation with the IUCN.
Jeong Eun-hae, Director General for International Cooperation Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “The WCC is an excellent opportunity to promote South Korea’s outstanding environmental policies and to enhance our influence in the international community as a key partner of the IUCN.” She added, “We will continue to expand cooperation in nature conservation through the IUCN and further strengthen South Korea’s standing in global environmental affairs.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Enforcement decree of the “Carbon Neutrality Framework Act” to take effect on October 23 following cabinet approval
▷ Expansion and reorganization of the “climate crisis monitoring and forecasting management system” to respond to abnormal and extreme weather, and establishment of the “integrated platform for climate crisis adaptation information” for comprehensive access to climate response information
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that the partial amendment to the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis (Carbon Neutrality Framework Act) was approved at the Cabinet meeting on October 14 and will take effect on October 23.
The amended enforcement decree includes provisions to actively respond to abnormal climate conditions and improve accessibility to climate crisis information by expanding and reorganizing the existing “weather information management system” into a “climate crisis monitoring and forecasting management system,” and establishing and operating an “integrated platform for climate crisis adaptation information.”
Under this amendment to the enforcement decree, the existing weather information management system will be expanded into a climate crisis monitoring and forecasting management system to respond to abnormal and extreme climate events. In addition, adaptation information scattered across different institutions will be unified and managed within the “integrated platform for climate crisis adaptation information.”
The Korea Meteorological Administration had established and operated a “weather information management system” to observe and forecast various weather phenomena. However, as the climate crisis has led to the frequent occurrence of abnormal and extreme weather events such as heavy rain, typhoons, heat waves, and cold waves, concerns have been raised that the current management system has limitations in effectively responding to the climate crisis.
Accordingly, through this amendment, an institutional foundation has been established to build and operate a climate crisis monitoring and forecasting management system that can monitor and predict abnormal and extreme weather events, identify the status of the climate crisis by region and sector, and present future trends of change.
In addition, an “integrated platform for climate crisis adaptation information” will be established and operated to collectively provide climate crisis adaptation information that had previously been offered separately by different institutions. This will enable industries, researchers, and the public to easily access and utilize the information in one place.
Through this, public accessibility to and utilization of climate crisis-related information, such as forecasts of heat waves, floods, and droughts, as well as changes in agricultural and fishery production and cultivation environments in response to these events, are expected to increase significantly.
For reference, the “integrated platform for climate crisis adaptation information” will begin with the water environment and marine and fisheries sectors this year and will be gradually developed in stages through 2028. It is also planned to provide customized information using an interactive artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot.
Oh Il-young, Director General for Climate and Energy Policy Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “This amendment to the enforcement decree has established an institutional foundation for proactively responding to the climate crisis.” He added, “We will continue to strengthen the foundation for climate crisis response in collaboration with the public and enhance the government’s execution capacity to achieve carbon neutrality goals.”
