▷ Presenting a blueprint for AI transformation in water management, including AI-based flood forecasting and water treatment plants
▷ From November 12 to 15, high-level officials and water management experts from more than 60 countries will participate
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) will hold the Korea International Water Week 2025 (KIWW) at EXCO in Buk-gu, Daegu, from November 12 to 15.
KIWW is the largest international water-related event in the country, held annually since 2016 to carry on the legacy of the 7th World Water Forum in 2015.
It is co-hosted by the MCEE, Daegu Metropolitan City, Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water), and Korea Environment Corporation, and organized by the Korea Water Forum.
Water management officials from more than 60 countries around the world, including high-level representatives* from the Cambodia’s Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology, Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation, Kenya’s Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation, Oman’s Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, Thailand’s Royal Irrigation Department, the American Water Works Association, and the Vietnam Water Supply and Sewerage Association, are expected to gather in one place.
* Thor Chetha, Minister of Water Resources and Meteorology of Cambodia; Abdraimov Aslan, Vice Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation of Kazakhstan; Julius Korir, Vice Minister of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation of Kenya; Ali Mohammed Zaher Al-Abri, Vice Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman; Suriyapong Nuchanon, Director-General of Thailand’s Royal Irrigation Department; Heather Collins, President of the American Water Works Association; and Tran Anh Tuan, Vice President of the Vietnam Water Supply and Sewerage Association.
Marking its 10th anniversary, this year’s event will be held under the theme “Smart Innovation: A Bridge to the Shared Water Future.” Over the course of three days, a total of 51 programs, including high-level meetings, special sessions, forums, competitions, and exhibitions, will address solutions to water challenges in the era of climate crisis.
According to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), 85% of climate-related disasters over the past 50 years have been water-related, such as floods, droughts, and heavy rainfall, showing that the climate crisis manifests most directly through water. In response, the government is presenting the “AI Transformation (AX) in Water Management” as a key solution to this year’s theme, “Smart Innovation.” This initiative aims to enhance safety and efficiency by utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) across all stages of the water cycle, including prediction, production, and supply.
First, in the prediction stage of water management, sessions such as the “Special Session on AI and Water Management” and the “Satellite Big Data Workshop” will showcase cases and outcomes of using AI and digital twins to advance flood forecasting and the management of dams and rivers. In particular, to promote the overseas expansion of related industries, the MCEE will sign a “Memorandum of Understanding on AI-Based Flood Forecasting Cooperation” with Kazakhstan on the first day of the event.
In the production stage of water management, the “Water Supply AI Transformation Symposium” will not only discuss strategies for transitioning water supply systems to AI-based management but also celebrate a milestone achievement, K-water’s “AI Water Treatment Plant” becoming the first in the world to receive international quality certification* (BDN) from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). This accomplishment follows its selection as a “Global Lighthouse” by the World Economic Forum (WEF) in 2023 and the approval** of an international standard draft by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), demonstrating the excellence of Korea’s AI-based water management technologies on the global stage.
* A key indicator referenced by global investors and multilateral development banks (MDBs) when assessing the reliability of infrastructure
** It is expected to be finalized as an international standard as early as 2026, following Technical Committee consensus and final approval voting.
The supply stage of water management is also being connected through AI. The “Special Session on Leakage Reduction” will discuss the effectiveness of smart pipeline network management technologies that apply AI, as well as strategies for overseas expansion, while also sharing local demand from Thailand, where there is a strong need for leakage reduction technologies. In addition, new technologies such as smart sewer and water pipeline inspection robots and smart flow measurement systems will be introduced, along with the vision of the Korea Water Cluster to support AI-based pilot projects in the water industry. Furthermore, the “Public-Private Partnership Conference on Digital and AI Water Industry” will be held on November 13, where cases of digital and AI-driven innovation will be shared.
In addition to AI, advanced technologies such as industrial wastewater reuse, hydropower generation, irrigation water systems, seawater desalination, and ultrapure water will be shared through special sessions to foster innovation. Furthermore, the Water EXPO held in the first-floor exhibition hall will feature innovative products and technologies from 71 companies and institutions.
International cooperation programs have also been further strengthened to ensure that such innovations serve as a bridge for all.
Starting this year, the “Global Partnership Forum Development Cooperation for Water Security” will be held for the first time, building on the global network accumulated through past events. This program brings together governments, development banks, and innovative companies to connect emerging project needs in water management with corresponding solutions. It is expected to evolve into a global platform where water-related challenges and solutions from around the world converge.
The MCEE will sign an MOU with Kenya’s Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation on November 12 to promote cooperation for sustainable water management and will further elaborate on specific collaboration measures through the “Kenya Water Security Cooperation Seminar” to be held on November 13. In addition, nine cities, including Mikkeli in Finland and Kumamoto in Japan, will participate in the “World Water Cities Forum” to share exemplary cases of urban water management solutions.
A variety of events will also be held to bring the international community together in shaping a shared water future.
At various events such as the “Water Leaders’ Round Table” and “Global Youth Bridge Builder,” leading figures and experts in the global water industry will share their professional insights for the benefit of future generations. In addition, discussions will be held on expanding the global initiative “Nationally Prepared Water Science Report*,” which Korea presented to the international community at the 2023 UN Water Conference, the first such conference held in 46 years.
*It provides a scientific foundation for presenting comprehensive and fundamental solutions to water-related issues.
In addition, the “TechXchange,” which supports the overseas expansion of Korean water companies, will operate throughout the event period. The Korea Water Cluster plans to sign water industry cooperation MOUs with major institutions in Kazakhstan and Vietnam. Export consultation sessions will also be held, inviting 12 organizations from countries such as Vietnam, Uzbekistan, and the Dominican Republic. Furthermore, side events will be organized to share Korea’s experiences and achievements with domestic and international visitors, including the screening of a video highlighting the 60-year history of Korea’s water management.
MCEE Vice Minister Kum Hanseung stated, “Marking its 10th anniversary, the KIWW will serve as a platform to demonstrate to the world how AI-based water management can provide concrete and powerful solutions to the global challenge of the climate crisis.” He added, “We hope this event will become the starting point of a new decade toward a sustainable water future, with Korea’s smart innovation in the water sector serving as a bridge.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Early launch of deployment programs and new-model effects push numbers past 200,000, with one million cumulative units expected early next year
▷ Continuing to identify effective support measures to help achieve the transport-sector target under the 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) while supporting domestic industry development
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that as of November 13, 2025, the number of electric vehicles (EV) supplied domestically this year has reached 200,000 units. This significantly surpasses the previous annual record of 164,000 units set in 2022.
Compared to 2021, when the annual supply of EVs surpassed 100,000 units for the first time, 10 years after the EV deployment program began in 2011, the annual supply has more than doubled in just four years, indicating that EV adoption is accelerating.
* (Annual EV supply) (2011-2016) 12,000 → (2017) 14,000 → (2018) 30,000 → (2019) 35,000 → (2020) 47,000 → (2021) 100,000 → (2022) 164,000 → (2023) 163,000 → (2024) 147,000 → (2025) 201,000 units (as of November 13)
By vehicle type, 172,000 electric passenger cars, 2,400 electric buses/vans, and 26,000 electric trucks have been supplied. The share of domestically produced vehicles is approximately 55% for passenger cars, 64% for buses/vans, and 93% for trucks.
In the case of electric buses (vans/buses), the domestic share fell to as low as 46% in 2023, but it has remained in the 63%-64% range in 2024 and 2025.
* (Domestic share of electric buses) (up to 2020) 68.3% → (2021) 61.5% → (2022) 58.1% → (2023) 45.8% → (2024) 63.3% → (2025) 63.7% (as of November 13)
Meanwhile, hydrogen vehicle deployment has also increased this year compared to the past two years (2023-2024). As a result, the combined cumulative number of electric and hydrogen vehicles has reached 950,000 units, and at this pace, it is expected to surpass one million early next year.
* (Annual hydrogen vehicle supply) (2020) 5,800 → (2021) 8,500 → (2022) 10,300 → (2023) 4,700 → (2024) 3,800 → (2025) 5,900 units (as of November 13)
This year’s increase in electric and hydrogen vehicle deployment is mainly attributable to the early launch of subsidy programs made possible by ing subsidy guidelines at the start of the year, as well as the “new-model effect” from manufacturers releasing a variety of new vehicles. In addition, charging infrastructure, which has improved both quantitatively and qualitatively in recent years*, appears to have influenced consumer preferences to some extent.
* (Fast chargers, cumulative) (up to 2020) 10,000 → (2021) 15,000 → (2022) 21,000 → (2023) 34,000 → (2024) 47,000 → (October 2025) 52,000 units(Slow chargers, cumulative) (up to 2020) 54,000 → (2021) 92,000 → (2022) 184,000 → (2023) 271,000 → (2024) 368,000 → (October 2025) 420,000 units
The MCEE has been carrying out EV and charging-infrastructure deployment projects since 2011, even before EVs entered full commercial use. It has also continuously refined the subsidy system to ensure that appropriate subsidies are provided in line with technological advancements and the release of new models by manufacturers.
In particular, through a subsidy policy that favors vehicles with strong performance and lower prices, the government is encouraging the release of models that align with consumer preferences. In response, the industry is working to continuously improve performance, such as single-charge driving range* and charging speed, while also striving to introduce more affordable, mass-market electric vehicles.
* (Key model driving range) (2011) BlueOn 140 km → (2016) Ioniq AE 190 km → (2018) Niro EV 385 km → (2025) EV4 550 km
The MCEE is restructuring and advancing the existing subsidy support system to maintain the expansion trend seen in 2025 and contribute to decarbonizing the transport sector in line with the 2030 and 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)* targets.
* (2035 transport-sector reduction target) 2018 emissions: 98.8 million tons → 2035: 36.8-39.3 million tons (a reduction of 60.2%-62.8%)
In addition, the Ministry plans to actively coordinate with relevant government agencies to identify more effective support measures and ensure that assistance reflects the broader ecosystem of domestic parts suppliers and related industries.
Minister Kim Sungwhan stated, “It is encouraging that EV deployment, the key driver of decarbonizing the transport sector, has grown significantly this year and gained accelerating momentum.” He added, “Going forward, we will work to ensure that the share of new electric and hydrogen vehicles exceeds 40% by 2030 and 70% by 2035, and we will strengthen support not only to increase the number of vehicles but also to enhance the overall competitiveness of Korea’s automotive industry and create jobs.”

▷ The 3rd K-Green Day green technology investor relations (IR) held in Silicon Valley, USA
▷ Linked with the Plug and Play Summit to pursue both tech exports and investment attraction
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that it will hold the 3rd K-Green Day Green Technology Investor Relations (K-Green Day @ Silicon Valley) on November 18 at the Plug and Play* Tech Center in Sunnyvale, Silicon Valley, USA.
* A world-renowned innovation and startup acceleration institution located in Sunnyvale, the heart of Silicon Valley in the United States.
This IR has been organized to strengthen the ability of domestic companies with outstanding technologies in promising green industry sectors to attract overseas investment and to establish a foundation for entering the U.S. market.
The United States is the world’s largest private investment market, with an excellent startup ecosystem in the environmental and energy transition sectors and highly active technology investment. Accordingly, since 2023 the MCEE has held the K-Green Day Green Technology Investor Relations annually in the U.S. (Silicon Valley), and this year’s event will be held in conjunction with the Plug and Play Silicon Valley November Summit*.
* A large-scale startup and investor event held each mid-November at the Plug and Play Tech Center headquarters in Sunnyvale, California, USA.
This year’s IR will bring together major U.S. venture capital firms, investors, and representatives of Korean companies operating locally to present the growth potential of Korean green technologies and discuss opportunities for investment cooperation.
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment selected 12 companies* to participate in the IR through an open call for companies wishing to attend.
* ABR, Recycle Ledger, EcoPeace, Repla, Light Bridge, WI Plat, aetech, DeepVisions, Carbon Energy, Turbine Crew, OZ Sepa, Tilda
To strengthen the capabilities of the participating companies, the ministry provided both group training and company-specific coaching on global green-industry investment market information and outlook, particularly for the United States, as well as on how to prepare materials and deliver effective presentations. This support helped the companies master presentation techniques suited to Silicon Valley’s culture and complete their pitch materials.
The companies participating this year possess technologies in fields that attract strong interest from U.S. investors, such as modular water-electrolysis systems for hydrogen energy production (Light Bridge), intelligent leak-management systems (WI Plat), and AI-based waste-sorting robots (aetech). As a result, their potential to secure investment connections on-site is drawing even greater attention.
In addition, during the IR, the Korea Environmental Industry Association and Plug and Play are scheduled to sign a Letter of Intent (LOI) to establish a mutual cooperation framework, which is expected to further strengthen support systems for Korean green companies seeking to enter the U.S. market.
Jung Eun-hae, Director General for International Cooperation Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “This event goes beyond a simple exhibition; it is a practical support system that strengthens both investment-attraction capabilities and global cooperation in the green industry sector.” She added, “We hope this becomes an opportunity for Korean green-technology companies to use the U.S. market as a foothold to rise as key players in the global green-industry ecosystem.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Agreement to cooperate on major projects, including a joint hyperscale AI data center project based on an energy mix
▷ Announcement of the bilateral “Strategic AI Cooperation Framework” and plans to establish working groups
The Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister Bae Kyunghoon), the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan), the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF, Minister Chun Jae-Soo), the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources (MOTIR, Minister Kim Jung-Kwan), and the Presidential Council on National Artificial Intelligence Strategy announced that, in connection with President Lee Jae-myung’s state visit to the UAE, the two countries will significantly expand bilateral cooperation across all fronts, including participation in the UAE Stargate Project*, the world’s largest artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure initiative.
* UAE Stargate Project: An AI data center (DC) cluster of up to 5 GW to be established in Abu Dhabi (with the first 200 MW-class AI cluster scheduled to begin operation in 2026).
The government has been strengthening the overall capabilities of the AI innovation ecosystem, spanning infrastructure, technology, and talent, through cooperation with BlackRock, OpenAI, and NVIDIA, in pursuit of becoming one of the “Global Top 3 in AI.” Aiming to become the “AI Capital of Asia,” Korea views strategic cooperation with key countries as essential to leading the fiercely competitive global market, and has therefore chosen to pursue AI and energy cooperation with the UAE as the first step. In other words, this cooperation with the UAE marks the first case of expanding Korea’s accumulated domestic capabilities into overseas markets and signifies that the Republic of Korea is now fully entering the global AI competition.
Regarding the Strategic AI Cooperation Framework
First, the two countries agreed to deepen comprehensive bilateral cooperation in the AI sector by signing the Strategic AI Cooperation Framework between Korea’s Presidential Council on National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (National AI Strategy Council), the highest decision-making body for AI policy in Korea, and Abu Dhabi’s Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council (AIATC). Priority areas of cooperation include AI investment and infrastructure development, expansion of AI supply chains, acceleration of AI and advanced technology adoption, and AI research and development. With the announcement of this framework, the two countries plan to cooperate extensively, from AI technology and application-service development to the construction of AI and energy infrastructure.
Beginning with this summit, the two countries agreed to jointly pursue large-scale projects aimed at mutual prosperity and development. As the first project, they decided to move quickly on the “Energy-Mix-Based Hyperscale AI Data Center Project.” This initiative includes building a large-scale AI data center in the UAE, establishing a power grid that utilizes nuclear energy, gas, and renewable energy to ensure stable operation, and expanding cooperation into the semiconductor supply chain sector.
The UAE Stargate Project is expected to involve initial investments of more than KRW 30 trillion, offering major opportunities for Korean companies, not only in climate-tech sectors such as energy, batteries, and eco-friendly solutions, but also for domestic AI startups and firms with experience in AI data centers, to participate in the global market.
Second, the two countries will pursue a “physical AI-based port and logistics project.” Leveraging Korea’s experience operating fully automated terminals and its data-driven physical AI technologies, the two sides plan to cooperate in building more efficient, automated, and intelligent ports. Korea and the UAE will carry out a joint project using Busan Port and Abu Dhabi’s Khalifa Port as test-bed ports for demonstration and validation. Transitioning to physical AI-based smart ports is expected not only to create growth opportunities for physical AI technology companies, but also to serve as a catalyst for spreading AI-driven port and logistics systems to major ports around the world. Through this cooperation, Korea and the UAE aim to establish an important milestone in their rise as global leaders in smart ports and logistics.
MoU on Exchanges and Cooperation to Expand Collaboration in the AI Sector
In addition, the MSIT signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the UAE Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence to expand bilateral cooperation in the AI sector. The MoU supports exchanges among research institutes, companies, and experts; promotes private-sector collaboration; and facilitates AI investment. Through this MoU, the two sides plan to pursue cooperation that encourages Korean AI companies to participate in the UAE’s AI data center development and AX projects. To ensure continued progress, the MSIT and the UAE Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence agreed to establish and operate a director-general-level AI Policy Consultative Body. This carries significance in strengthening cooperation channels for AI governance not only with Abu Dhabi but also with Dubai, reflecting the federal structure of the UAE government.
※ (Main points) To expand bilateral exchanges in the AI sector, the two countries will cooperate to: 1) conduct joint AI research, 2) facilitate exchanges between companies and experts, 3) share information related to AI regulatory sandboxes and certification, and 4) promote the participation of Korean companies in the establishment of the UAE’s AI data centers and in industry-specific AX projects.
Future Plans
To quickly implement the Strategic AI Cooperation Framework and generate tangible outcomes, the Korean government, led by the National AI Strategy Council, together with relevant ministries and agencies such as the MSIT, the MCEE, the MOF, and the MOTIR, as well as private-sector companies, will establish sector-specific working groups with the UAE side within the year. Through these working groups, the two countries will discuss concrete implementation measures and develop detailed cooperation plans.

text:
▷ Korea announces its 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) at the high-level segment of the 30th UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties
▷ In line with the national agenda to phase out coal, Korea declares its participation in the Powering Past Coal Alliance and hosts the “Climate and Clean Energy Transition Forum” to discuss a renewable-energy-centered transition with ministers from major countries
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that, on the occasion of its participation in the 30th UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP30), held in Belem, Brazil from November 10 to 21 this year (2025), it explored various avenues for cooperation with the international community to advance a decarbonized green transition.
First, Minister Kim Sunghwan presented Korea’s “2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)” to the international community during the high-level segment around midnight on November 18 (Korea time; 12:00 p.m. local time in Brazil). He expressed Korea’s commitment to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 and delivering a decarbonized green transition based on its target to reduce national greenhouse gas emissions by 53%-61% compared to 2018 levels.
In addition, he urged the international community to respond to the climate crisis through multilateral cooperation grounded in the spirit of Global Mutirao*, despite mounting uncertainties at the global level.
* Originating from an Indigenous Brazilian language, it means “collective cooperation.”
He also announced Korea’s decision to join the Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA), an international cooperation initiative aimed at achieving the phased phase-out of coal-fired power generation, at around 9:00 p.m. on November 17 (Korea time; 9:00 a.m. local time in Brazil).
This initiative provides a practical cooperation platform, such as policy exchanges and technical support, with the goal of phasing out coal-fired power generation. To date, more than 180 members (including national governments, local governments, and companies) participate in the alliance. In Korea’s case, eight local governments, including Chungcheongnam-do and Gyeonggi-do, have already joined.
Next, at 10:30 p.m. on November 17 (Korea time; 10:30 a.m. local time in Brazil), Minister Kim participated in the “Climate and Clean Energy Transition Forum,” where he shared policy visions for a renewable-energy-centered decarbonization transition with ministers from major countries. The event served as a platform to accelerate implementation of the agreement reached at COP28 to “triple global renewable power capacity and double energy efficiency.” It was co-hosted by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Energy Agency.
At the event, Australia’s Minister for Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water Chris Bowen; Portugal’s Deputy Minister for Energy Jean Barroca; and Denmark’s Climate Ambassador Ole Thonke participated in the thematic presentation session, engaging in discussions on the theme of “Achieving global carbon neutrality through a renewable-energy-centered energy transition.”
Minister Kim Sunghwan emphasized that “responding to the climate crisis is a challenge for all humanity, one that the global community, bound by a shared destiny, must confront together.” He added, “The Ministry will continue to work with the international community and actively participate in the global decarbonization transition so that Korea can become a leading nation in building a decarbonized green civilization.”

text:
▷ On-site engagement at POSCO’s hydrogen-based steelmaking facilities in Pohang and Hyundai Steel’s electric arc furnace-based production
▷ Inspection of Ulsan’s carbon capture and liquefaction (CCU) projects and bio-feedstock pretreatment plant
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that, to support the industrial sector’s transition to a decarbonized green civilization, it will hold on-site communication sessions with manufacturing facilities in Pohang and Ulsan, Korea’s leading industrial cities, on November 20.
As the first stop of the on-site engagement schedule, Ahn Se-chang, Deputy Minister of Climate and Energy Policy Breau at the MCEE, will visit the Pohang National Industrial Complex, home to leading global steelmakers POSCO and Hyundai Steel.
As of 2024, the steel industry accounts for 15% of Korea’s total net greenhouse gas emissions (approximately 651.4 million tons) and 40% of emissions from the industrial sector. As a major high-emission industry, the steel sector’s greenhouse gas reductions can determine whether the nation achieves its Nationally Determined Contribution.
In this context, POSCO is working to establish infrastructure for hydrogen-based steelmaking, while Hyundai Steel is attempting to reduce emissions by producing steel products primarily through electric arc furnaces rather than traditional blast furnaces.
Accordingly, Deputy Minister Ahn Se-chang will discuss with industry stakeholders ways to establish an eco-friendly steel production system in Korea. He will hear about POSCO’s and Hyundai Steel’s progress toward carbon neutrality and gather recommendations, including requests for government support to create demand for low-carbon steel products.
Next, Deputy Minister Ahn will inspect Approtium’s hydrogen production and carbon dioxide capture processes in Ulsan, a leading company in the hydrogen economy. Approtium supplies hydrogen to nearby refining and petrochemical complexes through a hydrogen pipeline network extending approximately 70 kilometers across the Ulsan area, supporting fuel switching in their operations.
In addition, the company is actively pursuing Carbon Capture & Utilization (CCU) projects, including capturing and liquefying carbon dioxide generated during hydrogen production and supplying it to semiconductor plants.
Deputy Minister Ahn plans to exchange views with Approtium on creating a decarbonized industrial ecosystem based on carbon capture and liquefaction, as well as on stabilizing hydrogen supply to accelerate carbon reductions in Korea’s high-emission industries. He will then inspect the bio-feedstock pretreatment unit (PTU)* at Ulsan New Port, which JC Chemical completed last month.
* Bio-feedstock pretreatment unit (PTU): A process that purifies low-grade bio-feedstocks, such as used cooking oil, palm by-products, and food-waste oils, into high-quality raw materials for Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF).
This process is an essential preparatory step for the refining industry to utilize bio-feedstocks as raw materials for sustainable aviation fuel, thereby reducing carbon emissions. JC Chemical is a company that has established domestic and international bio-feedstock supply chains to secure stable sourcing and high-quality processing, and also directly produces eco-friendly petroleum alternatives such as biodiesel. Deputy Minister Ahn plans to request the company’s active contribution to strengthening the full-cycle supply chain, ranging from securing bio-feedstocks to fuel production, for the decarbonization of the refining industry.
Deputy Minister Ahn Se-chang stated, “The government will actively support the industry’s transition of production processes to ensure that major emitting industries can maintain competitiveness while reducing carbon emissions.” He added, “We will strengthen policy support for technological innovation so that key low-carbon technologies, such as hydrogen-based steelmaking, biofuels, and carbon capture and liquefaction, can take root in industrial sites as quickly as possible.”

▷ Expanding cooperation with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates in water, resource circulation, and clean energy
▷ Strengthening climate response and green infrastructure cooperation, leading to overseas project opportunities for Korean companies
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that, from November 22 to 29, it will dispatch a “Green Industry Project Support Group” to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates.
This dispatch aims to strengthen intergovernmental cooperation and exchanges in the Middle East, where climate-change response and energy transition are accelerating, and to support overseas project bids by Korean green-industry companies. The support group will visit local governments and public procurement agencies to hold cooperation meetings, and will accompany Korean environmental and energy companies seeking to enter Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates to conduct technical consultations and present project proposals as part of practical bid-winning activities.
In Saudi Arabia, the support group will meet with officials from the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA), the National Water Company (NWC), and the Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) to discuss cooperation measures in water management and wastewater treatment that will support the implementation of “Vision 2030,” the country’s core national strategy.
“Vision 2030” is the Saudi government’s future blueprint aimed at moving away from an oil-dependent economic structure toward industrial diversification and sustainable growth.
The MCEE plans to strengthen institutional and diplomatic support so that Korean companies can secure competitive advantages in bidding for major new green-infrastructure projects linked to this strategy.
In addition, on November 23, a “Korea-Saudi Water Industry Cooperation Seminar” will be held with key local procurement agencies participating, where the two countries will share water-industry policies and innovative technologies, and conduct one-on-one business consultations.
In Kuwait, the “8th Korea-Kuwait Smart City Forum” will be held on November 26, hosted by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Kuwait.
The MCEE will co-host this event in cooperation with the overseas mission, introducing the technological capabilities and project-execution experience of Korean companies in connection with environmental infrastructure cooperation projects between the Kuwaiti government and the Korean government.
This event serves as an opportunity to advance concrete environmental-infrastructure cooperation between the two countries in relation to the Kuwait Abdullah New City construction project, and cooperation meetings with the Public Authority for Housing Welfare (PAHW) and the Environment Public Authority (EPA) of Kuwait will also take place on the same day.
At this meeting, the two governments will discuss the business conditions and cooperation measures for environmental infrastructure in the new city, such as wastewater treatment plants and waste-to-energy facilities, and will hold early-stage commercialization consultations aimed at moving toward practical project implementation in the future.
In the United Arab Emirates, the support group will strengthen the foundation for intergovernmental cooperation in the clean energy sector by holding meetings with major institutions such as the Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA).
The MCEE plans to provide diplomatic cooperation and support through official channels to ensure smooth progress in discussions on new green-hydrogen projects proactively proposed by Korean companies.
This round of consultations serves as a model for collaborative overseas project acquisition that combines governmental diplomatic support with private-sector technological capabilities, and is expected to reinforce the practical foundation for clean-energy cooperation between Korea and the United Arab Emirates.
Jung Eun-hae, Director General for International Cooperation Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “This Middle East dispatch is a representative example of policy-driven bid support that combines our companies’ green technologies with the government’s diplomatic capabilities,” adding, “In particular, the government-to-government (G2G) cooperation discussions with Kuwait and the clean-energy cooperation support with the United Arab Emirates are meaningful steps, as they link government-level cooperation to overseas project acquisitions for Korean companies.”
She added, “The government will continue to strengthen field-oriented support and international cooperation to ensure that Korean companies can steadily expand their green-industry exports.”

text:
▷ Vice Ministers Lee Hohyeon and Ryu Jemyung hold policy conference between the Climate Ministry and MSIT
▷ Discussion on cooperation measures for AI power supply, carbon neutrality, etc.
Lee Hohyeon, Second Vice Minister of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE), and Ryu Jemyung, Second Vice Minister of the Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), held a policy conference on November 21 (Fri) in Jung-gu, Seoul.
This meeting was convened to discuss the government’s global AI and energy cooperation efforts, such as Korea’s participation in the UAE Stargate initiative following the President’s state visit to the United Arab Emirates and the signing of an MoU with BlackRock, as well as to respond to rising power demand driven by AI industry growth at a time when public-private investment in AI infrastructure is accelerating, including the recent securing of 260,000 cutting-edge NVIDIA GPUs through APEC.
At the conference, the two ministries held in-depth discussions on policy cooperation measures related to AI and energy, including using AI to address climate change and achieve carbon neutrality, as well as building and expanding AI data centers. They also shared a strong consensus that securing a stable power supply is essential for strengthening the competitiveness of the AI industry. Accordingly, they exchanged views on related policy tasks such as: promoting the relocation of AI data centers outside the Seoul metropolitan area; revitalizing distributed energy special zones; reviewing approaches to data center power demand; improving regulations related to electricity; and enhancing global cooperation.
Vice Minister Ryu noted that AI has become a core element of national competitiveness, emphasizing that the two ministries will work together as one team to ensure AI infrastructure is built in a timely manner and will provide all necessary support so that AI can contribute to achieving carbon neutrality.
Vice Minister Lee emphasized that, while advancing the energy transition in line with the global trend of reducing carbon-based power generation, the government will make every policy effort to ensure a stable power supply in response to rising electricity demand from AI data centers through close cooperation between the two ministries.
Concluding the conference, the two vice ministers stated that the MSIT and the MCEE will continue close communication throughout the implementation of policies related to AI, electricity, and carbon neutrality. They also agreed to advance policy cooperation through various communication channels, from working-level meetings to vice-ministerial discussions, and plan to establish a joint AI-energy task force with industry participation in the near future.

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Final competition and awards ceremony for the “Startup Water 2025” to be held on November 25
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) and Korea Water Resources Corporation (President Yun Seogdae) announced that they will hold the final competition of the “Startup Water 2025” on November 25 at the Novotel Ambassador Hotel (located in Gangnam-gu, Seoul) to identify “innovative high-growth companies (unicorns)” that will drive the water industry as a new engine of growth for Korea.
As the importance of water management increases due to the intensifying climate crisis, the global water market is projected* to reach KRW 1,485 trillion in 2025.
What continues to drive this market, which grows steadily by 2.9% each year, includes: increasing investment in smart infrastructure; expanding demand for sustainable water-circulation technologies; and water-resource management technologies.
* Source: Global Water Intelligence (GWI)
Amid these global shifts, the MCEE considers the water industry a new growth engine that will lead the next decade. To identify startups and prospective founders with innovative technologies, it has hosted the Startup Water since 2020.
Now in its sixth year, the competition began with a nationwide call for applications on August 25 and was conducted in two categories: the “Idea Division” for the general public and the “Commercialization Division” for startup companies. A total of 80 teams entered the competition, and after rigorous document and presentation evaluations, 18 teams advanced to the finals.
The top four teams in each division will compete in the final round on November 25 before a panel of expert judges and a 52-member public evaluation group. Through this final evaluation, each division will select a Grand Prize winner, a First Prize winner, and two Excellence Award winners.
First, the companies that advanced to the final round in the Commercialization Division possess highly competitive, next-generation breakthrough technologies in high-demand global sectors such as ultrapure water and carbon capture.
These companies include: WaterTrinez, which has developed an eco-friendly filter that replaces fluoropolymer-based materials; K-Nano, which is developing an ultrapure-water purity monitoring system using artificial intelligence (AI) and particle engineering technologies; R&S Science, which provides a real-time monitoring system for low-molecular weight organic compounds such as urea; and Carbon Energy, which is developing core technology for direct air carbon capture using a seawater-based sodium electrolysis reactor.
The teams that advanced to the final round in the Idea Division showcase innovative technologies closely connected to everyday life.
Among these teams: Song A-yeong proposes a porous, resource-circulating water-quality and aquatic-ecosystem restoration block made from recycled marine waste; Choi Jong-yun presents a natural-drop, riverside microplastic-reduction technology using “RiverPresso,” an upcycled coffee-ground filter, both ideas that repurpose discarded waste for water management. Also noteworthy are ideas aimed at solving everyday water issues, such as: Lee Seung-hu’s commercialization concept for removing small organisms (chironomids) at water treatment plants using a microporous capture mesh, and Lee Sang-ho’s real-time water-security system based on a small language model (SLM).
Winners of this year’s competition will receive KRW 100 million in total prize money, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Award, and a comprehensive growth support package. The Ministry will provide recipients with integrated, practical support for commercialization, including: access to performance-testing facilities linked to the K-Testbed*; participation in domestic and international exhibitions for market expansion; and assistance in attracting investment through water-industry funds. Moreover, the Ministry plans to strategically connect the technologies and ideas presented in this competition with national R&D programs to accelerate innovation in the water sector.
* A support program that opens public- and private-sector facilities and equipment to startups and small and medium-sized enterprises, enabling them to conduct on-site validation of their innovative technologies and products and expand market access.
Meanwhile, over the past five years, the MCEE has discovered a total of 73 innovative startups through the Startup Water. As of last year, these companies recorded KRW 96.2 billion in sales, KRW 53.5 billion in investment attraction, and 464 new jobs created, establishing themselves as key players in Korea’s water-industry ecosystem.
Kim Hyojeong, Director General of Water Use Policy Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “With the global water market continuing to expand, now is precisely the time to actively nurture startups with innovative ideas and technologies.” She added, “The Ministry will continue to identify promising startups and prospective entrepreneurs and will be a strong supporter in helping them grow into real, successful businesses.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Five contributors to revitalizing the climate-energy new industry receive ministerial commendations
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim
Sungwhan) announced that it will hold the “2025 Climate Energy Tech Forum” on November 25 at the FKI Tower Conference Center in Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul.
The event, aimed at revitalizing the climate-energy new-industry ecosystem, will be attended by more than 100 participants including SMEs, start-ups, and investors. It will share trends in climate-energy policies and provide networking opportunities between outstanding companies and investors.
The event will begin with a keynote lecture by Professor Jung Soo-jong of Seoul National University, followed by presentations from financial institutions such as Korea Growth Investment Corporation and the Korea Technology Finance Corporation on investment trends in climate-energy technologies and financial support programs for innovative companies.
This will be followed by a second session featuring an investment briefing between climate-energy innovative venture companies and investors.
In addition, five individuals who have contributed to building and revitalizing the energy new-industry ecosystem will receive a Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment commendation for achievements including the development of an Energy Storage System (ESS) safety management system, the development of core technology for vanadium-ion batteries*, and the promotion of AI-based climate-adaptive agrivoltaics.
* A next-generation battery that can store and discharge electricity by repeatedly performing oxidation-reduction reactions using vanadium, a metal that can exist in four ionic states.
Seo Young-tae, Director General for Green Transition Policy Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “The growth of innovative companies that lead climate-energy technologies and new industries is more important than anything else in achieving a transition to a decarbonized green civilization.” He added, “We will continue to support collaborative platforms like this event to build a foundation for growth.”

text:
▷ Guidance on response measures for Korean exporters following recent amendments to relevant legislation
▷ On-site visit to Kos Limited to hear opinions on responses to the CBAM
The government held the 2025 5th briefing session on responses to the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) on November 26 at 2:00 PM at the Grand Hall of the Lahan Hotel in Pohang, Gyeongsangbuk-do, jointly with relevant ministries (Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources; Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment; Ministry of SMEs and Startups; Korea Customs Service) and related organizations.
At this briefing session, specific regulatory response measures were presented from the perspective of Korean export companies, based on the amended European CBAM legislation, which took effect on October 20. More than 100 industry representatives from the Yeongnam region, including companies exporting regulated items such as steel products, attended in person, and many additional companies participated online.
The government has been raising awareness of the CBAM and providing various forms of support through multiple channels to help Korean companies respond effectively. Through the export declarant notification program, businesses are informed when exporting regulated items, and guidance on the regulations and response measures is provided through joint briefing sessions and distribution of implementation manuals. For companies facing difficulties in calculating carbon emissions, expert consultations are available through the help desk (1551-3213), and capacity-building support is being offered through one-on-one customized consulting, automated emissions-calculation software, and hands-on training programs for responsible personnel.
Lee Jae-geun, Director General for New Trade Strategy and Policy at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources, stressed in his congratulatory remarks that “the government will make every policy effort domestically and internationally to ensure that foreign measures such as the CBAM do not act as trade barriers for Korean companies.” During a subsequent on-site visit to the Pohang plant of Kos Limited, following the briefing session, he stated, “Since industries such as steel, where carbon reduction is difficult, are becoming primary targets of global carbon regulations, the government will expand support to strengthen green competitiveness within the industry.”
The government plans to revise the CBAM implementation manual in line with the start of full enforcement and distribute it within the year. Going forward, it will continue to swiftly disseminate regulatory information and guidance on response measures, and will maintain ongoing consultations with relevant European Union authorities to ensure that the burden on Korean companies is minimized as additional subordinate regulations are announced.

text:
▷ Gathering expert and civil society input on key COP outcomes and climate issues... exploring ways to strengthen climate action and drive global climate leadership
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that it will hold the “Public Forum for the 30th Session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference of the Parties* (COP30)” on November 26 at Lotte Hotel in Jung-gu, Seoul.
* An international conference held annually to implement the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, adopted in 1992, and the Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, with approximately 50,000 participants including delegations from 198 Parties, private-sector experts, and civil society representatives (November 10-21, 2025, Belem, Brazil).
This event has been organized to share key negotiation outcomes from the COP30, collect opinions from experts and civil society on climate-related issues to strengthen Korea’s climate action, and explore ways to drive climate leadership in the international community.
The event will be held under two themes: "the outcomes of the Conference of the Parties and Korea’s implementation status on the 10th anniversary of the Paris Agreement," and "understanding and effectively utilizing the international carbon market." Each theme will include presentations, discussions, and a Q&A session.
The first theme, “Outcomes of the Conference of the Parties and Korea’s Implementation Status on the 10th Anniversary of the Paris Agreement,” will review the overall results of this year’s Conference of the Parties, examine negotiation outcomes on key agenda items such as the Global Goal on Adaptation and Just Transition, and discuss their implications for Korea.
The second theme, “Understanding and Effectively Utilizing the International Carbon Market,” will share trends in the international carbon market since the 29th Session of the Conference of the Parties (November 2024, Azerbaijan), where negotiations on the detailed implementation rules for Article 6 of the Paris Agreement were completed.
In addition, the session will explore ways to enhance domestic companies’ understanding of international greenhouse gas reduction projects by providing an overview of the detailed implementation guidelines for Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and the overall procedures for Korea’s international greenhouse gas reduction initiatives.
Jung Eun-hae, Director General for International Cooperation Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “Through this event, we will share the key outcomes of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change with the public in a timely manner to raise national awareness of climate crisis response and build consensus on the importance of climate action to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and the 1.5°C target.”
For further information, please contact the Public Relations Division.

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Government agencies and companies from Korea and Germany gather to discuss strengthening hydrogen cooperation
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that it will hold the “6th Germany-Korea Hydrogen Conference” on December 3 at KINTEX in Goyang, Gyeonggi-do, to share trends and discuss cooperation in the hydrogen economy among industry, academia, and research institutions from both countries.
This event is an annual academic forum jointly organized by Korea’s Hydrogen Alliance and Germany’s Fraunhofer Institute, among other organizations from both countries, to promote hydrogen cooperation among industry, academia, and research institutions. First held in 2020, it marks its sixth iteration this year.
Around 150 participants, including Axel Bree, Director for Hydrogen at the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy; Georg Wilfried Schmidt, Ambassador of Germany to Korea; officials and representatives from government and public organizations from both countries; hydrogen-related companies; and members of the research and academic sectors, will attend the event.
The event will be held across five sessions covering: hydrogen policy and market, hydrogen production, hydrogen storage and transport, hydrogen utilization, and hydrogen safety.
Presenters and panelists from relevant companies and institutions in both countries will participate to share trends across the entire hydrogen industry value chain and discuss cooperation measures such as building a hydrogen supply chain and technological innovation.
Park Deok-yeol, Director General for Hydrogen and Heat Industry Policy Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “Korea and Germany share common characteristics such as a manufacturing-centered industrial structure and a high dependence on energy imports, and are partners who must work closely together in achieving a hydrogen-economy ecosystem.”
He added, “By organically combining the industrial and technological capabilities that our governments and companies possess across the full cycle-from hydrogen production to distribution and utilization, and by strengthening cooperation in areas such as clean hydrogen supply chains and standards and certification, we will jointly contribute to the global expansion of the hydrogen economy.”

text:
▷ Strengthening cooperation through the 7th Energy Cooperation Committee and Energy Day Conference
▷ Discussing large-scale renewable energy deployment and grid integration for achieving carbon neutrality
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that it will hold the 7th Korea-Germany Energy Day Conference and the Korea-Germany Energy Cooperation Committee jointly with the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy on December 2 at Lotte Hotel in Jung-gu, Seoul.
Korea and Germany have held the annual Energy Day Conference and high-level Energy Cooperation Committee meetings based on the Korea-Germany Future Energy Cooperation Roadmap signed in 2020.
This Korea-Germany Energy Day Conference, under the theme “Large-Scale Renewable Energy Deployment and Grid Integration for Achieving Carbon Neutrality (Net Zero)”*, will discuss measures to accelerate the implementation of new large-scale renewable energy projects and to build out the power grid.
* A system that stably connects power sources such as solar and wind, whose energy output varies by time of day and weather, to the power grid and supplies electricity efficiently.
In particular, Korea will share its renewable-energy-centered “Korea Green Transformation (K-GX)” and decarbonization plans, while Germany, where the share of renewable energy is high, will share information on its own experiences and case studies.
This meeting will serve as a platform for cooperation based on public-private collaboration, with major German organizations such as RWE, Fraunhofer, Amprion, and Siemens participating alongside Korean institutions including the Korea Power Exchange, the Korea Wind Energy Industry Association, the Korea Energy Economics Institute, the Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning, the Korea Energy Agency, and the Korea Environment Institute, to explore new business opportunities.
At the Korea-Germany Energy Cooperation Committee to be held afterward, the two governments will introduce their energy transition policies and discuss mid- to long-term public-private cooperation strategies and measures for achieving climate and energy goals within the international community.
In the policy session, the two countries will share policies and experiences on expanding large-scale renewable energy deployment and continue in-depth discussions on industrial decarbonization and the phase-out of coal-fired power generation.
In the technology session, discussions will focus on potential areas for future cooperation centered on new green technologies such as green hydrogen, smart grids, and large-scale energy storage systems (ESS).
Jung Eun-hae, Director General for International Cooperation Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “Korea-Germany cooperation on the energy transition will contribute to joint efforts to achieve global climate and energy goals.” She added, “Continued cooperation between the two countries will accelerate decarbonization and the green transition.”

text:
▷ Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment to hold a “Roundtable on Development Strategies for Seawater Desalination” on December 4
▷ Leaders from construction, manufacturing, and industry, academia and research in the desalination sector gather in one place 
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that it will hold a “Roundtable on Development Strategies for Seawater Desalination” on December 4 at the Bizhub Seoul Center in Jung-gu, Seoul, to assess the current state of Korea’s seawater desalination industry and discuss future development directions.
The global seawater desalination market is projected* to expand from KRW 35 trillion in 2023 to KRW 73 trillion by 2032, growing at an average annual rate of 8.6%. This roundtable was organized to establish development strategies that will enable Korea’s seawater desalination industry to secure a leading position in the global market, which is rapidly expanding due to the worsening worldwide water shortage caused by the climate crisis.
* Fortune Business Insights, Global Desalination Technologies Market report (2024)
About 20 participants will attend the roundtable, including representatives from the MCEE, Korea Water Resources Corporation, Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute, Korea Water Partnership, as well as companies involved in seawater desalination and experts from research institutions and academia.*
* Samsung C&T, Hyundai Engineering & Construction, Doosan Enerbility, GS E&C, Techcross, Synopex, Hyorim E&I, CJK, DH Water, Korea Institute of Science and Technology, Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology, Kookmin University
At the event, the MCEE will present a draft development strategy for seawater desalination and a new national R&D plan, centered on: utilizing concentrated brine for resource recovery and carbon reduction; integrating renewable energy and improving energy efficiency; developing plants that can be rapidly transported and redeployed; and domesticating core materials, components, and equipment.
In the following discussion session, experts and companies will share their views on the proposed development strategy and R&D plan, and companies will relay the challenges they experience in the processes of R&D, demonstration, commercialization, and overseas expansion. Based on these insights, the discussion will address what concrete support the government should provide to revitalize the industry.
Kim Hyo-jeong, Director General for Water Use Policy Bureau at the MCEE, stated, “Securing a technological edge and strengthening competitiveness of Korean companies is essential for taking the lead in the rapidly growing global seawater desalination market driven by the climate crisis.” She added, “Based on the voices from the field discussed at this roundtable, we will devise practical development strategies that industry can genuinely feel.”

text:
▷ First Vice Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment attends the high-level segment of the Seventh Session of the United Nations Environment Assembly and presents Korea’s “decarbonized green transition” to steadily achieve its climate goals
▷ Emphasis placed on addressing the “triple planetary crisis,” including responding to the climate crisis as a “new driver of economic growth”
▷ Attends Oman’s “Sustainable Action” side event and proposes advancing toward “green cooperation” that goes beyond carbon-centered cooperation to jointly build a decarbonized green civilization
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that First Vice Minister Kum Hanseung will attend the high-level segment of the Seventh Session of the United Nations Environment Assembly*, to be held in Nairobi, Kenya, from December 11 to 12, as the head of the Korean delegation, where he will discuss “sustainable solutions for a resilient planet” with the international community.
* The Seventh Session of the United Nations Environment Assembly will be held from December 8 to 12 (with the Committee of Whole taking place from December 8 to 10).
The United Nations Environment Assembly is held every two years in Nairobi, Kenya, and is the highest-level environmental meeting at which ministers and vice ministers from UN member states convene to discuss the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)’s programme of work and budget and to adopt resolutions and declarations.
The Seventh Session of the United Nations Environment Assembly, themed “sustainable solutions for a resilient planet,” will bring together approximately 3,500 participants from around 160 countries, including ministers and vice ministers from each country, as well as representatives from international organizations, businesses, civil society, and non-governmental organizations.
Vice Minister Kum is expected to emphasize the significance of the establishment of the MCEE in his national statement at the high-level segment, underscoring Korea’s commitment to respond more proactively to the climate crisis and to emerge as a global leader in the transition toward a decarbonized green civilization.
In particular, he will introduce the “2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)” announced at the 30th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change last November, and express Korea’s firm commitment to steadily advancing decarbonization and green transition policies to achieve its climate goals.
* A reduction of 53%-61% compared to net greenhouse gas emissions in 2018
He will also outline key directions for addressing the “triple planetary crisis” of climate change, biodiversity loss and land degradation, and pollution. The plan is to leverage climate action as a new driver of economic growth by linking it with advanced industries such as artificial intelligence, while emphasizing the importance of expanding private-sector participation and diverse economic innovation instruments to conserve nature and enhance biodiversity. In addition, Korea will share its domestic circular economy strategies, such as Korean-style (K-) eco-design and the circular use of end-of-life electric vehicle batteries, to address plastic pollution, and will continue to expand related international cooperation.
Meanwhile, Vice Minister Kum will attend a side event hosted by Oman on the theme of “Sustainable Action” later that afternoon, where he will deliver a congratulatory address. In his remarks, he is expected to emphasize “green cooperation” that goes beyond carbon-centered cooperation such as natural gas and toward jointly building a global decarbonized green civilization.
First Vice Minister Kum Hanseung stated, “In an era of uncertainty, a decarbonized green civilization is a shared direction that humanity must pursue together.” He added, “The MCEE will work closely with the international community to ensure that the Republic of Korea establishes itself as a global leader in the decarbonized green civilization.”

text:
▷ First general committee meeting held for establishing the 12th Master Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand
▷ Open electricity plan created with public participation… early decision on nuclear policy direction through public discussion
▷ Minister Kim Sunghwan says the new plan is the cornerstone of energy transition… calls for active participation from committee members
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that on the afternoon of December 9, it will hold the first General Committee meeting to discuss the direction for establishing the “12th Master Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand (hereinafter the 12th Electricity Plan)” in the main conference room of the Government Complex Seoul, with Minister Kim Sunghwan in attendance.
The General Committee was formed with experts in the power sector, relevant organizations, and related government ministries to prepare the working draft of the 12th Electricity Plan.
At the meeting, the direction for establishing the 12th Electricity Plan, which was discussed at the 10th Electric Policy Council on November 27, will be shared with the members*, and opinions will be collected on the key areas that the General Committee should focus on.
* Refer to the November 27 press reference material on the launch of the “12th Master Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand.”
In addition, starting after the meeting, a working subcommittee* will be established under the General Committee to prepare tentative drafts for each sector, which will then be comprehensively reviewed by the General Committee and finalized as the working draft.
* ① Subcommittee on Demand Planning, ② Subcommittee on Facility Planning, ③ Subcommittee on Power System Innovation, ④ Subcommittee on Market Innovation, ⑤ Subcommittee on Jeju.
In particular, unlike the 11th plan, the 12th Electricity Plan will not establish working-level groups within each subcommittee. Instead, each subcommittee will discuss sector-specific issues from an integrated perspective, and continuous feedback will be ensured among the subcommittees, such as those on power supply planning, power system, and market, to maintain alignment.
In addition, considering the importance of expanding the power grid to support renewable energy deployment and to supply electricity to AI and advanced industries, a new Subcommittee on Power System Innovation will be established.
In his opening remarks, Minister Kim Sunghwan of the MCEE is expected to state, “The 12th plan will serve as the new administration’s first comprehensive energy plan and an important foundation for supporting Korea’s decarbonization, energy transition and industrial competitiveness,” while requesting the active participation of the committee members.
In particular, Minister Kim is expected to state, “The core of this electricity plan is an open, collaborative plan created through communication with the public,” and that “the new nuclear power plants included in the 11th Electricity Plan will be finalized early through a public opinion survey and national forum, and reflected in the 12th Electricity Plan.”
Minister Kim will also emphasize that “the forum will gather a wide range of opinions on the decarbonized power generation mix (energy mix) needed to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, as well as on addressing issues such as the intermittency of renewable energy and the inflexibility of nuclear power.”
He will also note that “the 12th plan must lay out a detailed blueprint for shifting from carbon-based generation to a renewable energy-centered system, while ensuring inherent power supply stability throughout the transition and guaranteeing the uninterrupted delivery of stable electricity to AI and advanced industries.”

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Final ation of rejection of the proposal to list all Anguilla species in CITES Appendix II
▷ Government delegation from the MCEE, the MOF, the MOFA, and the KFS contributes to biodiversity conservation and enhanced transparency in international trade
The government delegation (comprising the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE); the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF); the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA); and the Korea Forest Service (KFS), led by Chief Delegate Yoo Ho, President of the National Institute of Biological Resources (NIBR)) announced that the plenary session of the 20th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES*) successfully concluded on December 5 (local time) in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
It added that the proposal to list all species of the genus Anguilla (Anguilla spp.) in CITES Appendix II (Proposal No. 35), which Korea had actively addressed as a key agenda item, was ultimately not adopted, meaning the proposal was fully rejected.
The proposal, jointly submitted by the European Union (EU) and Panama, sought to strengthen international trade regulations for all species of the genus Anguilla. In the vote held on November 27, it was rejected by a wide margin, with 35 countries in favor, 100 opposed, and 8 abstaining. The decision was upheld at the current conference, ing the proposal’s final rejection.
The government delegation continued to monitor the movements of the proposing countries and held working-level consultations with partner nations in preparation for the possibility that the EU and Panama might seek to reopen the proposal after the vote on November 27, and up until the final ation at the plenary session on December 5.
As artificial seed production for eels is difficult in Korea, the country relies on imports for about 80% of the glass eels needed for aquaculture. Accordingly, the Korean government expressed opposition to the proposed listing due to concerns that, if adopted, it would lead to a sharp increase in transaction costs for glass eels. The rejection of the proposal to list all species of the genus Anguilla in CITES Appendix II is the result of securing broad support through bilateral and multilateral consultations with more than 40 Parties.
Meanwhile, Brazil proposed a complete ban on international trade (Appendix I) of Paubrasilia echinata, a material used for high-end string instrument bows, but through consultations the decision was adjusted to ban international trade only for wild specimens. In addition, it was agreed that CITES regulations will not apply, as before, when instruments made from this wood are moved across borders for non-commercial purposes.
In addition, a ban on international trade (Appendix I listing) was adopted for endemic species with limited distribution in certain countries, such as the okapi and the Chilean wine palm. A ban on international trade (Appendix I listing) was also approved for all species of manta rays and whale sharks, along with strengthened regulations for certain cartilaginous fish species such as some tope sharks.
This Conference of the Parties served as an opportunity for relevant ministries, including the MCEE, the MOF, the MOFA, and the KFS, to work organically together and effectively convey the Korean government’s scientific and responsible position to the international community. The government will continue to participate in international cooperation for the conservation and sustainable use of endangered species and plans to further strengthen inter-agency collaboration going forward.
The decisions adopted at the 20th CITES Conference of the Parties will soon be posted on the official conference website (cites.org), and unless otherwise specified, will take effect 90 days after the close of the meeting, on March 4, 2026. The MCEE plans to proceed without delay with domestic institutional adjustments, including the enactment of a notice concerning the national list of internationally endangered species.

text:
▷ International hydrogen event featuring an industry exhibition, conference, and various side programs
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (Minister Kim Sunghwan) announced that Minister Kim Sunghwan will attend the opening ceremony of the World Hydrogen Expo 2025, the largest hydrogen event in the Asia-Pacific region, which will be held at KINTEX (located in Ilsanseo-gu, Goyang-si) for seven days from December 4.
This event is expected to involve more than 280 companies and organizations from 26 countries around the world, and it will include a hydrogen industry exhibition, an international conference, and various side events.
In particular, since the Hydrogen Council General Assembly, a council of CEOs from more than 140 global hydrogen companies, will be held in Korea during the same week, a wide range of overseas hydrogen companies are expected to participate in the event.
At the exhibition, a wide range of items will be displayed, including technologies and products related to clean hydrogen production such as materials, components, and equipment for water electrolysis and ammonia cracking; hydrogen utilization products such as hydrogen buses, hydrogen electric trams, and hydrogen combustion engines; and various hydrogen distribution product lines including hydrogen refueling systems and liquefied hydrogen storage tanks.
The international conference will consist of three tracks* in which major governments such as Australia, Germany, and Japan, as well as international organizations including ISO and the International Partnership for Hydrogen and Fuel Cells in the Economy (IPHE), and overseas industry representatives will share the current status of the hydrogen economy and discuss international cooperation measures for expanding the ecosystem.
* 1. Leadership & Market Insight (high-level speeches by government and corporate leaders); 2. Hydrogen Deep Dive (presentations and discussions by domestic and international companies and experts; discussion on hydrogen technology development and industrial strategies); 3. Country Day (country-specific discussions on the hydrogen industry)
Various side programs to support companies will also take place. Through events such as technology and product briefings for domestic hydrogen companies, export consultation meetings, and the “H2 Innovation Award,” which selects innovative technologies and companies in the hydrogen sector, the event will support corporate technology and product promotion as well as overseas market entry.
Minister Kim Sunghwan stated at the opening ceremony, “Following the recent announcement of the ‘2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)’ to the international community at the 30th UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties, the government plans to fundamentally transform the industrial and economic structure through the transition to green industry in Korea. We will systematically support the establishment of a hydrogen ecosystem, which is a key means of industrial innovation and decarbonization.” He added, “I hope this event will serve as an opportunity to revitalize the global hydrogen industry ecosystem and to showcase the innovative technologies and products of Korean companies to the global market.”
For further information, please contact the Public Relations Division.

Phone: +82-44-201-6055
Email: gcjgina @gmail.com

title: Press Release
text:
▷ Minister Kim Sungwhan of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment attends the Jeonnam offshore wind power completion ceremony and offers encouragement
The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE, Minister Kim Sungwhan) announced that Minister Kim Sungwhan will attend the completion ceremony of Jeonnam Offshore Wind Power* Phase 1, to be held on December 11 at Ramada Plaza by Wyndham Jaeundo (located in Sinan-gun, Jeollanam-do).
* SK Innovation E&S-Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners joint venture
Jeonnam Offshore Wind Power Phase 1 is a 96 MW offshore wind farm located approximately 9 km off the coast of Jaeundo, Sinan-gun, and is the first offshore wind power project to be selected under the competitive wind power bidding system introduced in 2022.
This project is the first privately led offshore wind power project in Korea and is regarded as a model case in which various regulations and competing interests, such as military operations consultations and local community acceptance, were successfully addressed through public-private cooperation among the central government, local governments, and the project developer.
In addition, by being carried out as a community participation project, a portion of the power generation revenues is shared with local residents, and many local companies from areas such as Sinan and Mokpo took part in the construction process, making it a model of regional co-prosperity that demonstrates how offshore wind projects can contribute to revitalizing the local economy.
Minister Kim Sungwhan stated, “Offshore wind power is a key instrument for the transition to a decarbonized green civilization, and the completion of Jeonnam Offshore Wind Power Phase 1 will serve as a catalyst for the future expansion of offshore wind power in Korea.” He added, “In line with the policy tasks set out in the plan to expand offshore wind infrastructure and deployment jointly announced by relevant ministries on December 10, we will faithfully implement these measures to accelerate the deployment of offshore wind power nationwide and actively support the industry so it can move into a phase of full-scale growth.”
